**Section 2.3 --- Tax Treatment**

The Partnership and the General Partner intend that the Reorganization be treated for U.S. federal income tax purposes as follows, and the General Partner is authorized to take all actions and make all elections consistent with the following intended tax treatment:

> \(a\) **Tax-Free Contributions Under IRC § 721(a).** The Step 4 Contributions constitute tax-free contributions of property to the Consolidated Master Fund in exchange for partnership interests under IRC § 721(a), and no gain or loss shall be recognized by Fund V-A Cayman, Fund V-B Lux, or any of their respective partners as a result of such contributions.
>
> \(b\) **Carryover Basis and Holding Period Tacking.** The Consolidated Master Fund\'s basis in the portfolio company assets received in the Step 4 Contributions shall be determined under IRC § 723, which provides for a carryover basis equal to the adjusted tax basis of such assets in the hands of the contributing partnerships immediately prior to the contribution. The Consolidated Master Fund\'s holding period in such assets shall include the holding period of the contributing partnerships under IRC § 1223(2).
>
> \(c\) **Not an Investment Company.** The Consolidated Master Fund is not an \"investment company\" within the meaning of IRC § 721(b) and Treasury Regulations § 1.351-1(c)(1)(ii), as the portfolio of the Consolidated Master Fund consists of interests in operating companies engaged in digital infrastructure (data centers, fiber-optic networks, edge computing) and enterprise SaaS businesses, and the Consolidated Master Fund does not hold a diversified portfolio of stocks, securities, or other investment assets of the type described in IRC § 351(e)(1).
>
> \(d\) **IRC § 367 Inapplicable.** Sections 367(a) and 367(b) of the Code do not apply to the Step 4 Contributions because the Consolidated Master Fund is classified as a partnership, and not as a corporation or an association taxable as a corporation, for U.S. federal income tax purposes pursuant to the Form 8832 entity classification election filed in connection with Step 1 of the Reorganization.
>
> \(e\) **Tax-Free Distributions Under IRC § 731(a).** The Step 5 distributions of Consolidated Master Fund partnership interests by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles to their respective limited partners constitute tax-free distributions under IRC § 731(a), and no gain shall be recognized by the distributing partnerships or by the distributee partners, except to the extent that money distributed exceeds the adjusted basis of the distributee partner\'s interest in the distributing partnership (which the General Partner does not anticipate will occur). Section 731(c) of the Code does not apply to the Step 5 distributions because the Consolidated Master Fund partnership interests distributed are not \"marketable securities\" as defined in IRC § 731(c)(2), as such interests are not traded on an established securities market and are not readily tradable on a secondary market or the substantial equivalent thereof.
>
> \(f\) **IRC § 704(c) Built-In Gain Tracking.** Built-in gain and loss accounts under IRC § 704(c) applicable to the portfolio company assets held by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles shall carry over to the Consolidated Master Fund and shall be maintained and tracked by the Consolidated Master Fund using the remedial allocation method described in Treasury Regulations § 1.704-3(d), which is the same method that has been used by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles and the Partnership.
>
> \(g\) **IRC § 752 Liability Shifts.** Shifts in partner-level shares of the aggregate \$1,340,000,000 in liabilities that will be assumed by or transferred to the Consolidated Master Fund in connection with the Reorganization shall be netted under Treasury Regulations § 1.752-1(f) and are not expected to result in the recognition of gain by any partner, as the increases and decreases in each partner\'s share of partnership liabilities occurring as part of the Reorganization are treated as occurring simultaneously rather than sequentially.
>
> \(h\) **No IRC § 1446 Withholding.** No withholding under IRC § 1446(a) is required with respect to the Step 4 Contributions or the Step 5 distributions, as the Step 4 Contributions are tax-free contributions that do not give rise to effectively connected taxable income allocable to foreign partners, and the Step 5 distributions are tax-free distributions under IRC § 731(a).
>
> \(i\) **PLR Request Authorization.** The General Partner is authorized to seek confirmation of the foregoing intended tax treatment through the PLR Request to the IRS Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries), and to take all actions reasonably necessary to prosecute and advance the PLR Request to a favorable conclusion.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Fund V parallel vehicle portfolio assets being contributed to the Consolidated Master Fund in the Step 4 Contributions include interests in 12 portfolio companies, with specific reference to the following key holdings: (i) Veridian Edge Computing Corp. (fair market value of approximately \$1,120,000,000; adjusted tax basis of approximately \$780,000,000; built-in gain of approximately \$340,000,000); and (ii) Helix SaaS Holdings Ltd. (fair market value of approximately \$445,000,000; adjusted tax basis of approximately \$310,000,000; built-in gain of approximately \$135,000,000). The complete schedule of portfolio company interests, including fair market values, adjusted tax bases, and built-in gains, will be set forth in the contribution agreements and the exhibits to the PLR Request.

**Section 2.4 --- Scope of Authorization**

The authorization granted to the General Partner pursuant to this Article II extends to actions taken prior to, on, or after the Effective Date in furtherance of the Reorganization. Any actions taken by the General Partner prior to the Effective Date that were within the scope of the authorization granted by this Article II are hereby ratified and confirmed.

The General Partner may modify the timing of the Reorganization steps described in the Recitals, provided that the target effective date for the Step 5 Dissolutions remains on or about December 1, 2025, or such other date as the General Partner determines in its reasonable discretion, taking into account the progress of the PLR Request, the receipt of lender consents, the availability of regulatory approvals, and other relevant factors. The General Partner shall provide the LPAC with reasonable advance notice of any material changes to the Reorganization timeline.

The General Partner may adjust the structure of the Reorganization as reasonably necessary to address feedback received from the IRS during the pre-submission conference (which has been requested for July 22, 2025) or in response to the PLR Request, or to address changes in applicable tax law, regulation, or administrative guidance, provided that such adjustments do not materially adversely affect the economic rights, investment exposure, or tax position of the Limited Partners. If any structural adjustment is required that would, in the General Partner\'s reasonable judgment, materially adversely affect the Limited Partners, the General Partner shall seek LPAC consent prior to implementing such adjustment.

**[ARTICLE III --- AMENDMENTS TO THE PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Amendment to Investment Provisions**

The Partnership Agreement is hereby amended to permit the Partnership\'s portfolio company assets that are held through Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux (i.e., the portfolio company interests held indirectly by the Partnership through the Legacy Offshore Vehicles as part of the parallel fund structure) to be contributed to the Consolidated Master Fund as part of the Reorganization. For the avoidance of doubt, this amendment authorizes the transfer of such assets out of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles and into the Consolidated Master Fund, notwithstanding any investment restrictions, transfer limitations, or other provisions in the Partnership Agreement that might otherwise be interpreted to restrict or prohibit such transfers.

Following the consummation of the Reorganization, the Partnership (Fund V LP) will co-invest alongside the Consolidated Master Fund on a proportionate basis, rather than alongside separate parallel offshore vehicles. All new investments and follow-on investments of the Partnership shall be made in accordance with this co-investment arrangement, with Fund V LP investing directly and the feeder vehicles investing indirectly through the Consolidated Master Fund.

The existing investment restrictions, concentration limits, sector allocation guidelines, and diversification requirements set forth in the Partnership Agreement shall continue to apply to the Partnership\'s investments, and for purposes of measuring compliance with such restrictions and limits, the Partnership\'s investments shall be calculated on an aggregated basis that includes both the Partnership\'s direct investments and the Partnership\'s proportionate share of the Consolidated Master Fund\'s investments. The General Partner shall ensure that the limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund contains investment restrictions that are consistent with, and no less restrictive than, the investment restrictions set forth in the Partnership Agreement.

**Section 3.2 --- Amendment to Parallel Fund Provisions**

All provisions in the Partnership Agreement relating to the parallel fund structure, specifically those provisions governing the establishment, maintenance, and operation of parallel fund vehicles alongside Fund V LP, and the relationship between Fund V LP and the Legacy Offshore Vehicles, are hereby amended to reflect the post-Reorganization structure.

Following the consummation of the Reorganization, all references to \"Parallel Funds,\" \"Parallel Vehicles,\" or similar terms in the Partnership Agreement shall be deemed to refer to the Consolidated Master Fund, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder, and not to the Legacy Offshore Vehicles (which will have been dissolved pursuant to Step 5 of the Reorganization).

The aggregate investments convention pursuant to which investment opportunities are allocated on a proportionate basis across Fund V LP and its parallel vehicles shall be maintained through the Consolidated Master Fund structure. The General Partner shall ensure that the limited partnership agreement of the Consolidated Master Fund and the limited partnership agreements of the feeder vehicles contain provisions that are consistent with the aggregate investments convention and the principles of proportionate allocation applicable under the Partnership Agreement.

**Section 3.3 --- Amendment to Allocation and Distribution Provisions**

The allocation and distribution provisions of the Partnership Agreement, including the provisions governing the allocation of net income, net loss, capital gains, and capital losses among the Partners, and the provisions governing the distribution of proceeds and other amounts to the Partners, are hereby amended to the extent necessary to accommodate the following:

> \(a\) The Consolidated Master Fund structure as a co-investment vehicle alongside Fund V LP, such that the allocation and distribution provisions of the Partnership Agreement operate in a manner that is economically equivalent to the allocations and distributions that would have been made under the prior parallel fund structure;
>
> \(b\) The continuation of IRC § 704(c) built-in gain and loss tracking for the contributed properties using the remedial allocation method under Treasury Regulations § 1.704-3(d), including the maintenance of § 704(c) accounts at the Consolidated Master Fund level and the flow-through of § 704(c) allocations to the Partners through the feeder structures; and
>
> \(c\) Adjustments to IRC § 752 liability allocations resulting from the Reorganization, including the reallocation of liability shares among the Partners to reflect the post-Reorganization structure.

For the avoidance of doubt, the existing distribution waterfall, carried interest provisions, management fee provisions, preferred return calculations, clawback obligations, and all other economic terms of the Partnership Agreement remain unchanged except to the extent specifically and expressly modified by this Amendment to reflect the post-Reorganization structure. The General Partner shall ensure that the economic terms of the Consolidated Master Fund\'s limited partnership agreement are structured to preserve the economic equivalence of the Partnership\'s existing terms for all categories of investors.

**Section 3.4 --- Amendment to Transfer and Withdrawal Provisions**

The transfer restrictions and withdrawal provisions in the Partnership Agreement are hereby amended to permit the limited partner migration contemplated in Step 5 of the Reorganization without requiring the individual transfer consent procedures that would otherwise apply under the Partnership Agreement. Specifically:

> \(a\) The migration of non-U.S. limited partners from Fund V-A Cayman to the International Feeder shall not be treated as a \"transfer\" requiring the General Partner\'s consent or the satisfaction of any other transfer conditions under the Partnership Agreement; and
>
> \(b\) The migration of U.S. tax-exempt limited partners from Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Lux to the Tax-Exempt Feeder shall not be treated as a \"transfer\" requiring the General Partner\'s consent or the satisfaction of any other transfer conditions under the Partnership Agreement.

Any admission of a Limited Partner or former limited partner of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles into the International Feeder or the Tax-Exempt Feeder in connection with the Reorganization shall not be treated as a new admission, a transfer, or a secondary transaction requiring consent under the Partnership Agreement. For all purposes of the Partnership Agreement and the Reorganization Documents, such migrations and admissions shall be treated as part of the integrated Reorganization transaction and shall not give rise to any transfer fees, consent fees, or other charges that might otherwise be assessed in connection with transfers or admissions under the Partnership Agreement.

**Section 3.5 --- Amendment to Reporting and Information Rights**

The reporting obligations of the General Partner under the Partnership Agreement are hereby amended to include the Consolidated Master Fund as a vehicle through which the Partnership\'s parallel investments are made following the Reorganization. Without limiting the foregoing:

> \(a\) The General Partner shall provide the Limited Partners with quarterly and annual financial statements and reports that reflect both (i) Fund V LP\'s direct holdings and (ii) Fund V LP\'s proportionate share of the Consolidated Master Fund\'s holdings, presented in a manner that provides the Limited Partners with a comprehensive view of the Partnership\'s total investment portfolio;
>
> \(b\) The General Partner shall cause the Consolidated Master Fund to prepare and maintain books, records, and financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (\"GAAP\"), subject to the same accounting policies and practices applicable to Fund V LP;
>
> \(c\) FATCA (IRC §§ 1471--1474), CRS, and all other tax information exchange reporting obligations shall be prepared and filed in a manner consistent with the post-Reorganization structure, with the objective of simplifying and streamlining the reporting obligations across the Solara fund platform; and
>
> \(d\) Annual Schedule K-1s and all other tax reporting materials shall be prepared in a manner that accurately reflects the post-Reorganization structure, including the flow-through of items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit from the Consolidated Master Fund through the feeder vehicles to the individual Partners.

**Section 3.6 --- Amendment to LPAC Provisions**

The LPAC provisions of the Partnership Agreement are hereby amended to reflect that the LPAC\'s oversight and consent authority extends to matters involving the Consolidated Master Fund, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder insofar as such matters affect the Partnership, the Limited Partners, or the economic terms of their investment in the Partnership.

Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP (Diana Carruthers, Partner) shall continue to serve as outside counsel to the LPAC and shall provide independent advice to the LPAC with respect to matters arising under the Consolidated Master Fund structure and the feeder vehicles.

The preliminary consent provided by the LPAC at the meeting held on April 22, 2025, at which Limited Partners holding approximately 78% in interest of the capital commitments to the Partnership voted in favor of the Reorganization, is hereby confirmed and ratified. Such consent shall be deemed to satisfy any LPAC consent requirements under the Partnership Agreement with respect to the Reorganization, including the formation of the new entities, the Step 4 Contributions, the Step 5 Dissolutions, and the related limited partner migrations.

**Section 3.7 --- Amendment to Dissolution Provisions**

The dissolution provisions of the Partnership Agreement are not amended by this Amendment. Fund V LP shall continue as a separate Delaware limited partnership and is not dissolved, merged, or terminated as a result of the Reorganization. The term of the Partnership, and all provisions governing the winding up and dissolution of the Partnership, shall remain in full force and effect.

For the avoidance of doubt, the dissolution of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles under Step 5 of the Reorganization does not constitute a dissolution event with respect to Fund V LP under the Partnership Agreement, does not trigger any dissolution or termination provisions of the Partnership Agreement, and does not give rise to any right of any Limited Partner to withdraw from the Partnership or to receive a distribution of such Limited Partner\'s capital account balance in lieu of continuing participation in the Partnership.

**[ARTICLE IV --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Representations and Warranties of the General Partner**

The General Partner hereby represents and warrants to the Limited Partners as of the Effective Date as follows:

> \(a\) **Power and Authority.** The General Partner has full power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under this Amendment and to cause the Partnership to consummate the Reorganization on the terms and conditions described herein. The General Partner is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware.
>
> \(b\) **Due Authorization.** The execution and delivery of this Amendment by the General Partner and the consummation of the Reorganization have been duly authorized by all necessary limited liability company action on the part of the General Partner, including the approval of the board of the General Partner obtained at a duly convened meeting held on March 14, 2025, and no further action on the part of the General Partner is required to authorize this Amendment or the Reorganization.
>
> \(c\) **Binding Obligation.** This Amendment constitutes the legal, valid, and binding obligation of the General Partner, enforceable against the General Partner in accordance with its terms, except as such enforceability may be limited by applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, or similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and by general principles of equity.
>

# I. Executive Summary

FATCA/CRS Compliance Simplification: Consolidated reporting reduces complexity and compliance risk across multiple jurisdictions
Governance Simplification: LP-requested streamlining of parallel fund governance, voting, and reporting across multiple vehicles

# V. Tax Treatment — Overview of Rulings Requested
Ruling 1 (§ 721): Tax-free contributions of portfolio assets to Master Fund LP — no gain/loss recognized
Ruling 2 (§ 721(b)): Master Fund LP does not constitute an 'investment company' (operating company portfolio)
Ruling 3 (§ 367): §§ 367(a)/(b) do not apply — provisions apply only to transfers to/from corporations, not partnerships
Ruling 4 (§ 731): Tax-free distributions of Master Fund LP interests to LPs upon dissolution of legacy vehicles

Ruling 6 (§ 704(c)): Built-in gain/loss accounts carry over; remedial allocation method continues
Ruling 7 (§ 1446): No withholding required on contributions or distributions (nonrecognition transactions)
Ruling 8 (Entity Classification): All new entities properly classified as partnerships under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3

<!-- Slide number: 11 -->
# Ruling 1: IRC § 721(a) — Tax-Free Contributions
Each offshore vehicle contributes its entire portfolio to Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP in exchange for a limited partnership interest
Under IRC § 721(a), no gain or loss is recognized by the contributing partnerships or their partners on the contribution of property to a partnership
Carryover basis under IRC § 723 — Master Fund takes the same tax basis as the contributing vehicle
Holding period of contributed assets tacks under IRC § 1223(2)
No cash boot or other consideration beyond partnership interests

<!-- Slide number: 12 -->
# Ruling 2: IRC § 721(b) — Not an Investment Company
IRC § 721(b) denies tax-free treatment if the contribution results in 'diversification' and the partnership is an 'investment company'
Treas. Reg. § 1.351-1(c)(1)(ii) defines 'investment company' by reference to holdings of 'stocks, securities, or other investment assets'
Solara's portfolio consists entirely of operating company interests — digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS platforms
All 23 portfolio companies are active operating businesses, not passive investment assets
Conclusion: § 721(b) exception does not apply; contributions remain tax-free

<!-- Slide number: 13 -->
# Rulings 3–4: § 367 Inapplicability & § 731 Distributions
Ruling 3 (§ 367): IRC §§ 367(a) and 367(b) by their terms apply only to transfers to or from corporations — the Master Fund LP is a partnership; § 367 does not apply
Ruling 4 (§ 731): Distributions by legacy vehicles of Master Fund LP interests to LPs in Step 5 are tax-free under § 731(a) — no gain recognized because LPs receive only partnership interests, not money
IRC § 731(c) marketable securities exception does not apply — Master Fund LP interests are not 'marketable securities' as they are not actively traded or readily tradable on a secondary market

<!-- Slide number: 14 -->
# Rulings 5–6: Liability Shifts (§ 752) & Built-In Gain Carryover (§ 704(c))
Ruling 5 (§ 752): $1.34B in aggregate liabilities shift from legacy vehicles to Master Fund LP — §§ 752(a)/(b) create deemed contributions and distributions as partner shares change
Netting under Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) and tiered partnership rules applied to demonstrate no net gain recognition under § 731
Ruling 6 (§ 704(c)): $1.72B in built-in gain accounts carry over from legacy vehicles to Master Fund LP
Master Fund LP will continue to use the remedial allocation method under Treas. Reg. § 1.704-3(d) for each contributed property
Ensures historic investors continue to bear their appropriate share of built-in gain on eventual disposition

<!-- Slide number: 15 -->
# Rulings 7–8: Withholding (§ 1446) & Entity Classification
Ruling 7 (§ 1446): No withholding on Steps 2–4 contributions or Step 5 distributions — nonrecognition events generate no effectively connected taxable income
Particularly relevant for non-U.S. investors (Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund, Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group)
Ruling 8 (Entity Classification): Master Fund LP, International Feeder, and Tax-Exempt Feeder each properly classified as partnerships under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3 via check-the-box elections
Form 8832 elections to be filed for each new entity with effective dates coordinated to precede the first contribution step

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Counselors at Law* One Vanderbilt Avenue, 44th Floor New York, New York 10017

Telephone: (212) 814-6000 Facsimile: (212) 814-6001 www.calderwoodharkness.com

October 9, 2023

**VIA EMAIL AND HAND DELIVERY**

Ardent Capital Management LLC 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022

> Attention: Marcus Aldridge, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
>
> Priya Narayanan, Co-Founder & Managing Partner

Dear Mr. Aldridge and Ms. Narayanan:

We are pleased to confirm the engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") by Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"ManCo\" or the \"Client\") to serve as legal counsel in connection with the matters described herein. This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions upon which we will provide legal services to the Client in connection with this engagement.

**[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter confirms that Calderwood & Harkness has been engaged by the ManCo to serve as legal counsel in connection with a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in total commitments. The ManCo is a Delaware limited liability company and a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") under CRD #298417. The Fund\'s sole general partner is Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company.

The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.

**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

The engagement will comprise the following principal workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. We understand that the scope of the engagement may evolve as the restructuring progresses; any material expansion of the scope described herein will be discussed with the Client in advance.

**2.1 Entity Restructuring**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the restructuring of the organizational hierarchy of the Ardent Capital platform, including:

\(a\) Advising on the formation of a new Delaware limited liability company, to be named Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\"), which will serve as a parent holding company for both the General Partner and the ManCo, thereby consolidating the principals\' economic interests and governance rights in a single vehicle at the top of the organizational structure.

\(b\) Advising on the formation of an intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\"), as a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo and the sole member of the General Partner. GP Intermediate will serve as an interposing entity between HoldCo and the General Partner, facilitating the allocation of carried interest economics and providing structural flexibility for the admission of future principals and the potential establishment of successor funds.

\(c\) Drafting and negotiating limited liability company agreements for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including provisions governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, distribution waterfalls, governance (including voting and consent requirements), transfer restrictions, withdrawal and removal mechanics, non-compete and non-solicitation covenants, and such other provisions as may be appropriate.

\(d\) Preparing amended and restated limited liability company agreements for the General Partner and the ManCo to reflect the new holding-company structure, including modifications to membership interest provisions, management and officer provisions, and capital account and allocation provisions necessitated by the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate.

\(e\) Preparing and filing Certificates of Formation with the Delaware Secretary of State for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, together with any ancillary filings or registrations required in connection with the formation and qualification of such entities.

\(f\) Preparing Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the \"LPA\") to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner, including any required modifications to the definitions, representations, and governance provisions of the LPA necessitated by the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo above the General Partner.

**2.2 Economics Realignment**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the reallocation and documentation of the economic arrangements among the principals of the Fund, including:

\(a\) Advising on the reallocation of carried interest percentages and management fee profit-share allocations among the remaining and next-generation principals, taking into account the departure of the principals described in Section 2.3 below, the contributions of continuing principals, and the Firm\'s understanding of the Client\'s objectives with respect to the incentivization and retention of key personnel.

\(b\) Drafting an amended and restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement reflecting the revised carried interest percentages applicable to each principal, including vesting schedules, forfeiture and clawback provisions, and mechanics for the allocation of carried interest among HoldCo members through the GP Intermediate and General Partner chain.

\(c\) Drafting a Management Fee Sharing and Profit Allocation Agreement at the HoldCo level, setting forth the allocation of management fee revenue among HoldCo members, including base compensation allocations, discretionary bonus pools, and distribution priorities.

\(d\) Revising the co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal group and to address any changes in co-investment rights and priorities resulting from the restructuring.

**2.3 Departing Principal Separation**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the negotiation and documentation of separation arrangements for two departing principals:

\(a\) **David Kellner** (Senior Partner), who is retiring from the Ardent Capital platform; and

\(b\) **Joanna Trask** (Partner), who is departing voluntarily.

In connection with each departing principal, the Firm will:

> \(i\) Draft comprehensive separation and release agreements, addressing, among other things, the departing principal\'s resignation from all positions with the ManCo, the General Partner, HoldCo (if applicable), and all affiliated entities; mutual releases of claims; confidentiality, non-disparagement, non-solicitation, and (as applicable) non-competition covenants; cooperation obligations; and any ongoing compensation or benefits arrangements.
>
> \(ii\) Draft carry retention and clawback side letters, specifying the portion of carried interest to be retained by each departing principal with respect to investments made during his or her tenure, the clawback obligations applicable thereto, and the mechanics for the calculation and payment of any retained carry distributions.
>
> \(iii\) As applicable, draft a senior advisor agreement in favor of Mr. Kellner, setting forth the terms of any ongoing advisory role, including the scope of services, compensation, expense reimbursement, and termination provisions.
>
> \(iv\) Coordinate, as necessary and appropriate, with Whitford & Chase LLP, counsel to the departing principals, led by Richard Beaulieu, Esq., in connection with the negotiation and finalization of all separation documentation.

**2.4 LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on all limited partner notification, consent, and compliance matters arising from the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Preparing materials for notification to, and solicitation of consent from, the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, including a detailed memorandum describing the restructuring and its implications for the Fund and its limited partners.

\(b\) Analyzing compliance with the Fund\'s fourteen (14) existing side letters, with particular attention to key-person provisions under Section 5.2 of the LPA and any expanded or supplemental key-person provisions contained in certain side letters, to determine whether the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask or the structural changes contemplated by the restructuring trigger key-person events, consent requirements, or notification obligations under any such side letter.

\(c\) Preparing LP notification letters to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund, describing the restructuring, the changes to the General Partner structure, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, and any other information required to be disclosed under the LPA or the applicable side letters.

\(d\) Advising on the preparation and filing of an amended SEC Form ADV (Parts 1 and 2) to reflect the restructuring, and advising on any other regulatory filings or notifications required in connection with the restructuring, including any applicable state regulatory filings.

**2.5 Tax Structuring**

Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax analysis and structuring advice in connection with the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Federal income tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including the tax treatment of the contribution or transfer of interests in the General Partner and the ManCo to HoldCo.

\(b\) Delaware tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including any applicable Delaware franchise taxes, formation taxes, or annual reporting obligations.

\(c\) Federal income tax analysis of the reallocation of carried interest among the principals, including the application of Section 1061 of the Internal Revenue Code and any implications arising from the modification of existing partnership interests.

\(d\) Tax analysis of the economic arrangements with departing principals, including the characterization of carry retention payments and the tax treatment of any consideration paid in connection with the separation arrangements.

\(e\) Section 704(b) and Section 704(c) analysis of built-in gain allocations with respect to existing Fund investments, including the impact of the restructuring on the allocation of built-in gains and losses among the principals and the mechanics for tracking and allocating such amounts through the revised entity structure.

\(f\) All tax structuring advice under this engagement will be provided by Sylvia Hartwell, Specialist Partner (Tax), who will coordinate as necessary with the Client\'s independent accountants at Heathrow Whitman & Co.

**2.6 Limitations on Scope**

The scope of this engagement is limited to the matters described in Sections 2.1 through 2.5 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the following matters are expressly excluded from the scope of this engagement:

\(a\) Routine fund operations, portfolio company transactions, and ongoing limited partner communications unrelated to the restructuring described herein. We understand that such matters will continue to be handled by Pemberton Hale LLP (Victoria Langford, Partner), which serves as the Fund\'s existing fund formation and operations counsel.

\(b\) Accounting, auditing, and valuation services, which we understand are provided by Heathrow Whitman & Co. (accountants and auditors) and Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation), respectively. Nothing in this engagement shall be construed as the provision of accounting, auditing, or valuation advice by Calderwood & Harkness.

\(c\) Representation of any departing principal, including David Kellner and Joanna Trask, in connection with the restructuring or any other matter. Each departing principal is separately represented by Whitford & Chase LLP.

\(d\) Representation of any limited partner of the Fund in connection with the restructuring or any other matter.

To the extent matters arise during the course of this engagement that fall outside the scope described herein but that may benefit from our involvement, we will discuss with the Client whether and on what terms such matters should be added to the scope of this engagement or addressed through a separate engagement.

**[3. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

The following attorneys will serve as the primary members of the engagement team:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Name**                **Role**                   **Responsibility**
  ----------------------- -------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Nicholas Stern          Responsible Partner        Overall supervision of the engagement, strategic advice, and senior-level involvement in key negotiations and decision points

  Graham Sutherland       Billing Partner            Billing, engagement administration, and fee-related communications

  Owen Fischer            Lead Associate             Day-to-day management of the engagement, including document drafting and negotiation, coordination with counterparty counsel (Whitford & Chase LLP) and other advisors (Pemberton Hale LLP, Heathrow Whitman & Co., Broadleaf Consulting Group)

  Stephen Adler           Working Associate          Document drafting, due diligence, preparation of regulatory filings, and research support

  Sylvia Hartwell         Specialist Partner (Tax)   Tax structuring advice, Section 704(b) and 704(c) analysis, and coordination with Heathrow Whitman & Co. on tax-related matters
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

From time to time, additional attorneys or paraprofessionals may be assigned to the engagement as the Firm deems necessary or appropriate to ensure efficient and timely completion of the workstreams described herein. The Client will be notified in advance of any such additions to the engagement team.

**[4. Fee Arrangement and Billing]{.underline}**

**4.1 Hourly Rates**

Fees for services rendered in connection with this engagement will be charged on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Timekeeper Level**                **Hourly Rate**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Partner                             \$1,650

  Specialist Partner                  \$1,750

  Senior Associate                    \$950

  Associate                           \$750
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The foregoing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each year. In the event of any rate adjustment during the term of this engagement, the Firm will communicate such adjustment to the Client in advance. Adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of the adjustment.

**4.2 Estimated Fee Range**

Based on the anticipated scope and complexity of the engagement as described in Section 2 above, and taking into account the number of workstreams, the anticipated volume of document drafting and negotiation, and the extent of LP consent and regulatory compliance work expected to be required, we estimate that total professional fees for this engagement will fall within the range of **\$850,000 to \$1,100,000**.

This estimate is provided solely for budgeting purposes and does not constitute a cap, ceiling, or fixed fee. Actual fees may vary from this estimate based on a number of factors, including (without limitation) the ultimate scope and complexity of the work, the nature and duration of negotiations with Whitford & Chase LLP on behalf of the departing principals, the extent and complexity of LP consent solicitation and side-letter compliance matters, the number and complexity of tax structuring issues that arise, and any expansion of the scope of the engagement beyond the matters described herein. The Firm will endeavor to keep the Client informed on an ongoing basis of any circumstances that are likely to cause total fees to exceed the upper end of the estimated range, and will discuss with the Client any potential modifications to the scope or approach to the engagement that might mitigate such costs.

**4.3 Disbursements.** In addition to professional fees, the Client will be responsible for reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred by the Firm in connection with the engagement. Disbursements may include, without limitation, filing fees (including Delaware Secretary of State filing fees for Certificates of Formation and other filings), messenger and courier charges, travel expenses (including transportation, lodging, and meals incurred in connection with travel reasonably necessary for the engagement), document production and reproduction costs, computerized legal research charges, and similar items. All disbursements will be itemized on the Firm\'s monthly invoices.

**4.4 Billing Procedures**

Invoices for professional fees and disbursements will be rendered monthly. All invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Invoices will be directed to:

> Ardent Capital Management LLC 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022
>
> Attention: Finance Department

Copies of all invoices will also be provided to Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan at the address set forth above, or at such other address or electronic mail address as the Client may designate in writing from time to time. The Client agrees to notify the Firm promptly if there is any question or dispute regarding any invoice, so that any such matter may be addressed in a timely manner.

**[5. Client Identity and Conflicts]{.underline}**

The Client for purposes of this engagement is Ardent Capital Management LLC. Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and will not be deemed to represent, any individual principal of the Fund (including, without limitation, Marcus Aldridge, Priya Narayanan, or any other continuing principal), any departing principal (including David Kellner and Joanna Trask), any limited partner of the Fund, or any other entity in the Ardent Capital structure (including, without limitation, the Fund, the General Partner, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, or any portfolio company) in their individual or separate capacities. Each such person and entity should consult with its own independent legal counsel with respect to any matter in which its interests may differ from those of the ManCo.

The Firm has conducted a conflict check in accordance with its standard procedures and, as of the date hereof, has identified no conflicts of interest that would preclude this engagement. In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of the engagement, the Firm will promptly notify the Client and take appropriate action, which may include seeking an informed written waiver of the conflict from the affected parties or, if a waiver cannot be obtained or is not appropriate under the circumstances, withdrawing from the representation in whole or in part as required by applicable rules of professional conduct.

**[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by or on behalf of the Client in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s professional obligations and applicable rules of professional conduct. This obligation of confidentiality extends to all non-public information concerning the Fund, the General Partner, the ManCo, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, the principals (whether continuing or departing), the limited partners, the portfolio companies, and any other entities or persons about which information is provided to the Firm in connection with the engagement.

The Firm may disclose confidential information as required by applicable law, regulation, or court order, or with the prior written consent of the Client. In the event the Firm receives a subpoena, court order, or other compulsory process seeking the disclosure of confidential information relating to this engagement, the Firm will, to the extent permitted by law and practicable under the circumstances, provide prompt notice to the Client prior to making any such disclosure, so that the Client may seek protective measures or take other appropriate action.

**[7. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will retain engagement files, including correspondence, memoranda, agreements, and other documents generated or received in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, as in effect from time to time. Upon completion or termination of the engagement, the Firm will, at the Client\'s request and expense, return original documents to the Client or make arrangements for the transfer of files. Documents retained by the Firm may be destroyed in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy following the expiration of the applicable retention period, unless the Client requests in writing that such documents be returned or otherwise preserved.

**[8. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter and the terms and conditions set forth herein shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to the conflict-of-laws principles thereof.

**[9. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. In the event of termination by either party, the Client will remain responsible for payment of all professional fees earned and disbursements incurred through the date of termination, in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in Section 4 above.

Upon termination, Calderwood & Harkness will take reasonable steps to protect the Client\'s interests, including cooperating in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Client. The Firm will promptly deliver to the Client or its successor counsel all documents and materials necessary for the continued handling of the matter, subject to the Firm\'s right to retain copies of such documents in accordance with its document retention policy and applicable rules of professional conduct.

**[10. Acceptance and Counterparts]{.underline}**

We respectfully request that the Client confirm its acceptance of the terms and conditions of this engagement by having each of the undersigned representatives execute and return the enclosed copy of this Engagement Letter to Calderwood & Harkness at the address set forth above, or by transmitting an executed copy by electronic mail to Nicholas Stern at nstern@calderwoodharkness.com or Graham Sutherland at gsutherland@calderwoodharkness.com.

This Engagement Letter may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) or by other electronic transmission shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.

We look forward to working with you and the Ardent Capital team on this important matter. Please do not hesitate to contact either of us if you have any questions regarding the terms of this engagement or if you would like to discuss any aspect of the representation in greater detail.

Very truly yours,

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**

Nicholas Stern Partner

Dear Ms. Loomis:

We are delighted to set forth the terms pursuant to which Calderwood & Harkness LLP (the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" \"us,\" or \"our\") will represent Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC (\"HCP\" or the \"Client\") in connection with the formation and fundraise of the Client\'s fifth flagship private equity fund, as described in greater detail below. This letter (this \"Engagement Letter\"), when countersigned by the Client, shall constitute the binding agreement between the Firm and the Client with respect to the engagement described herein.

**[1. Engagement and Client Identification]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm its engagement by Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, in connection with the formation, structuring, and fundraise of the Client\'s fifth flagship private equity fund and the related fund vehicles described in Section 2 below (collectively, the \"Engagement\"). HCP will serve as the Sponsor and promoter of the fund and its related vehicles, and in that capacity is responsible for all aspects of the fundraise, investor relations, and fund management.

We note that HCP is a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC File No. 801-79223; CRD No. 298417) and is subject to the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended, and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

For purposes of this Engagement, HCP is the sole client of the Firm. Although we will be forming and advising on various related entities in the course of the Engagement --- including the fund partnership entities, the general partner entity, the blocker corporation, and the offshore feeder vehicle, each as identified in Section 2 below --- HCP is the sole entity to which we owe a duty of loyalty and professional responsibility. We do not represent, and will not be deemed to represent, any limited partner, prospective limited partner, placement agent, lender, fund administrator, or any other third party in connection with this matter. Each such third party should engage its own legal counsel as it deems appropriate.

**[2. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

The scope of our Engagement encompasses the following workstreams, each as more fully described below. Matters that fall outside the scope of this Section 2 are excluded from the Engagement unless separately agreed in writing.

**2.1 Fund Vehicles to Be Formed**

We will form and structure the following entities in connection with the fundraise (collectively, the \"Fund Complex\"):

**(a) Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP (\"HPE Fund V\" or the \"Fund\")** --- a Delaware limited partnership that will serve as the main fund vehicle for the fifth flagship private equity fund. The target hard cap for capital commitments to HPE Fund V is Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000).

**(b) Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC (the \"General Partner\")** --- a Delaware limited liability company to be organized as the sole general partner of HPE Fund V and the Parallel Fund. The sole member of the General Partner shall be HCP.

**(c) Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP (the \"Parallel Fund\")** --- a Delaware limited partnership to be organized as a parallel vehicle for the investment by certain tax-exempt and non-U.S. limited partners that may require alternative structuring to address specific tax, regulatory, or policy considerations. The Parallel Fund will invest on a substantially pari passu basis alongside the Fund.

**(d) Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP (the \"Offshore Feeder\")** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to be organized as a feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors seeking to invest through a non-U.S. jurisdiction. Subject to the exclusion described in Section 2.10 below, our work with respect to the Offshore Feeder will be limited to the drafting of the exempted limited partnership agreement under New York law governing provisions, with Cayman Islands formation filings and CIMA registration to be handled by local Cayman counsel engaged by the Client.

**(e) HGF V blocker Corp. (the \"Blocker\")** --- a Delaware C corporation to be organized as a blocker entity through which certain tax-exempt investors may invest in the Fund Complex in order to mitigate exposure to unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\").

**2.2 Core Formation Work**

In connection with the formation of the Fund Complex, we will perform the following work:

> \(a\) Drafting and negotiating the Agreement of Limited Partnership of HPE Fund V LP (the \"LPA\"), which shall set forth the terms and conditions governing the formation, governance, investment activities, capital contributions, distributions, allocations, management fees, carried interest, expenses, reporting obligations, and dissolution of the Fund.
>
> \(b\) Drafting the Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Parallel Fund, which shall contain terms and conditions substantially consistent with the LPA, adapted as necessary to accommodate the particular tax, regulatory, and structural considerations applicable to the Parallel Fund\'s investor base.
>
> \(c\) Drafting the Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement of the Offshore Feeder, which shall contain terms and conditions consistent with the LPA, adapted as necessary for the Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership structure and the particular requirements of non-U.S. investors.
>
> \(d\) Drafting the Limited Liability Company Agreement of the General Partner, which shall set forth the governance, capitalization, and operating terms of the General Partner entity.
>
> \(e\) Preparing and filing the Certificate of Limited Partnership for HPE Fund V LP with the Delaware Secretary of State, Division of Corporations.
>
> \(f\) Preparing and filing the Certificate of Formation for Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC with the Delaware Secretary of State, Division of Corporations.
>
> \(g\) Preparing and filing the Certificate of Incorporation for HGF V blocker Corp. with the Delaware Secretary of State, Division of Corporations.
>
> \(h\) Drafting the Bylaws of HGF V blocker Corp., including provisions governing the board of directors, officers, indemnification, and corporate procedures.

**2.3 Offering Documents**

We will prepare the following offering and subscription documents for the Fund Complex:

> \(a\) Drafting and negotiating the Confidential Private Placement Memorandum (the \"PPM\") for HPE Fund V LP, which shall describe the investment strategy, key fund terms, risk factors, tax considerations, regulatory disclosures, track record information for predecessor funds (HPE Fund I through HPE Fund IV), biographies of key investment professionals, and other material information required in connection with the private placement offering.
>
> \(b\) Drafting the form Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire for each vehicle in the Fund Complex (i.e., the Main Fund, the Parallel Fund, and the Offshore Feeder), which shall include customary investor representations, warranties, and certifications (including accredited investor, qualified purchaser, ERISA, FATCA, and anti-money laundering certifications).
>
> \(c\) Drafting the Investor Suitability Questionnaire / Know Your Customer (\"KYC\") Form, incorporating current anti-money laundering and sanctions screening requirements applicable to the Fund Complex.

**2.4 Side Letters and LP Negotiations**

We will perform the following work in connection with side letter negotiations with prospective limited partners:

> \(a\) Preparing a form Side Letter template containing standard concession provisions commonly requested by institutional limited partners, including without limitation provisions addressing most favored nation (\"MFN\") rights, enhanced reporting and transparency requirements, co-investment allocation rights, transfer and secondary sale provisions, ERISA-related representations and covenants, and tax-related provisions (including withholding and allocation matters).
>
> \(b\) Negotiating individual side letters with anchor and institutional limited partners and their respective counsel. As of the date hereof, the following investors and their counsel have been identified as likely participants in the side letter negotiation process:
>
> \(i\) Northmoor State Pension System (counsel: Aldworth & McBride LLP);
>
> \(ii\) The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund (counsel: Pelham Chambers LLP);
>
> \(iii\) Edgecombe Insurance Group Ltd.;
>
> \(iv\) Velthorn Family Office LLC;
>
> \(v\) Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority (counsel: Ramsden Clarke International LLP); and
>
> \(vi\) Stonewall Partners Fund of Funds III LP.
>
> Additional investors and their counsel will be identified as the fundraise progresses, and we will negotiate side letters with such investors as directed by the Client.
>
> \(c\) Preparing the form MFN Election Notice to be distributed to all limited partners entitled to elect the benefit of MFN-protected side letter provisions following each closing.

**Please note:** All work described in this Section 2.4, including the negotiation of individual side letters with limited partners and their respective counsel, will be billed on an hourly basis at the rates set forth in Section 5.1 below and is **outside** the Fee Cap described in Section 5.2 below. This carve-out reflects the inherently unpredictable nature of side letter negotiations, which are driven by the number of investors, the complexity of their requests, and the responsiveness of their counsel. Estimates of anticipated side letter negotiation costs will be provided to the Client as specific LP negotiations commence.

**2.5 Tax Structuring**

Our tax practice will advise on the following matters in connection with the formation and structuring of the Fund Complex:

> \(a\) Advising on the partnership tax classification of the Main Fund and the Parallel Fund under Subchapter K of the Code (Sections 701--777), including confirmation of classification as partnerships for U.S. federal income tax purposes and analysis of relevant elections.
>
> \(b\) Analyzing UBTI considerations for tax-exempt limited partners (including charitable organizations, pension plans, university endowments, and other exempt entities) and advising on the role and structure of the blocker entity in mitigating UBTI exposure under Sections 511--514 of the Code.
>
> \(c\) Analyzing effectively connected income (\"ECI\") and Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act (\"FIRPTA\") withholding issues for non-U.S. investors investing through the Offshore Feeder and/or the Main Fund, including analysis of Sections 1445 and 1446 of the Code and applicable income tax treaty provisions.
>
> \(d\) Advising on compliance with Section 1061 of the Code, including the application of the three-year holding period requirement for carried interest (applicable profits interest) received by HCP and its investment professionals in connection with the Fund Complex.
>
> \(e\) Analyzing the Cayman Islands tax neutrality of the Offshore Feeder, including consideration of the economic substance requirements under Cayman Islands law and the absence of Cayman Islands income tax, capital gains tax, or withholding tax applicable to the Offshore Feeder and its partners.
>
> \(f\) Preparing written tax structuring memoranda for the Client summarizing the foregoing analyses and providing recommendations regarding the optimal tax structure for the Fund Complex.
>
> \(g\) Preparing the ERISA Analysis Memorandum, which shall analyze the benefit plan investor percentage threshold under 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101(f) (as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA) and advise on procedures and monitoring mechanisms to ensure that the assets of the Fund are not treated as \"plan assets\" under ERISA --- i.e., that benefit plan investors hold less than 25% of the value of each class of equity interests in the Fund (excluding interests held by the General Partner and its affiliates).

**2.6 Regulatory and Compliance**

We will advise on the following regulatory and compliance matters:

> \(a\) Preparing and filing Form D (Notice of Exempt Offering of Securities) with the SEC within fifteen (15) days of the First Close of the Fund, in accordance with the requirements of Regulation D under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the \"Securities Act\"), Rule 506(b).
>
> \(b\) Coordinating state blue sky notice filings in all U.S. states and territories where limited partners are domiciled, as required by applicable state securities laws. > \(d\) Advising on Investment Advisers Act compliance matters as applicable to the fundraise, including consideration of advertising and performance presentation requirements, Form ADV disclosure updates, and custody rule compliance.

> \(e\) Preparing the Placement Agent Disclosure & Compliance Memorandum regarding Osprey Capital Markets LLC, which has been engaged by the Client as the placement agent for the Fund. This memorandum will address compliance with SEC guidance on placement agent disclosures, state pay-to-play restrictions, and Rule 206(4)-5 under the Investment Advisers Act (political contributions and placement agent regulations for government entity investors).

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Attorneys at Law*

600 Lexington Avenue, 38th Floor New York, New York 10022

Telephone: (212) 554-8000 Facsimile: (212) 554-8001 www.calderwoodharkness.com

May 12, 2025

**VIA EMAIL AND Sundial Data Systems**

Priya Narasimhan, Esq. General Counsel Solara Digital Infrastructure LP 1200 Market Street, Suite 3400 Wilmington, Delaware 19801

> **Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Private Letter Ruling Request in Connection with Cross-Border Fund-Platform Reorganization of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP**
>
> **Engagement Number: 20250527-SDILP-PLR**

Dear Ms. Narasimhan:

**[1. Purpose and Acceptance]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (\"Solara\" or \"SDILP\"), a Delaware limited partnership, and its general partner, Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (\"Solara GP\"), a Delaware limited liability company (collectively, the \"Client\"), to provide the legal services described in this engagement letter (this \"Letter\"). We appreciate the confidence that Solara and Solara GP have placed in our Firm, and we look forward to working with your team on this significant and complex matter.

This Letter sets forth the terms and conditions upon which Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services in connection with the matter described herein. By countersigning this Letter in the space provided below, the Client agrees to be bound by the terms and conditions set forth herein. This engagement shall be effective as of the date of the countersignature below. No attorney-client relationship will be deemed to have been established with respect to the matter described herein until this Letter has been signed by an authorized representative of the Client and returned to the Firm.

**[2. Description of the Client]{.underline}**

The client for this engagement is Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (EIN: 82-4917366) and Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (EIN: 82-4917365). For the avoidance of doubt, the \"Client\" as used throughout this Letter refers collectively to SDILP and Solara GP, except where the context clearly requires otherwise.

Solara is a Delaware-based private equity sponsor with approximately \$14.7 billion in assets under management as of March 31, 2025, operating across digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS verticals. Solara sponsors private equity funds through a series of parallel fund structures established across Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and Luxembourg to accommodate U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt, and non-U.S. investor pools. The fund platform reflects a multi-jurisdictional architecture that is common among institutional-scale private equity sponsors and is central to the reorganization that is the subject of this engagement.

The principal contact persons at Solara for purposes of this engagement are as follows:

> • **Priya Narasimhan**, General Counsel --- primary legal contact and authorized decision-maker for engagement-related matters;
>
> • **Stefan Dalmqvist**, Head of Tax --- primary contact for substantive tax matters, financial data, and coordination with the Client\'s independent auditors and valuation advisors.

The Managing Partner and Founder of Solara is **Viktor Raines**. Mr. Raines will serve as the authorized officer of Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC for purposes of executing any penalties of perjury declarations and other representations required in connection with Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") submissions, as described more fully in Section 8 below.

All communications from the Firm regarding this engagement should be directed to Ms. Narasimhan and Mr. Dalmqvist, unless otherwise instructed in writing by the Client.

**[3. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

**3.1 Overview of the Transaction**

Solara is undertaking a cross-border reorganization of its fund platform (the \"Reorganization\"), involving the domestication and merger of several Cayman Islands and Luxembourg fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure. The Reorganization is designed to simplify the Client\'s fund architecture, reduce administrative and operational costs, enhance investor reporting, and achieve certain tax efficiencies in connection with the ongoing management and eventual disposition of portfolio company interests.

The Reorganization involves the following existing fund vehicles (collectively, the \"Legacy Fund Vehicles\"):

> \(i\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$4.2 billion in committed capital (vintage 2021), approximately 72% deployed as of the date hereof;
>
> \(ii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$1.85 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors;
>
> \(iii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.15 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.24 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for certain European institutional investors;
>
> \(iv\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$5.6 billion in committed capital (vintage 2023), approximately 38% deployed as of the date hereof;
>
> \(v\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$2.45 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; and
>
> \(vi\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.38 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.49 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for certain European institutional investors.

The Reorganization contemplates the formation of the following new entities (collectively, the \"New Fund Vehicles\"):

> \(i\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership to serve as the master fund in a restructured master-feeder architecture;
>
> \(ii\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company to serve as the general partner of the Consolidated Master Fund;
>
> \(iii\) **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors; and
>
> \(iv\) **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for U.S. tax-exempt investors.

The Reorganization involves a multi-step transaction that includes, among other things, asset contributions by the four offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the dissolution of the legacy offshore vehicles following such contributions, and the migration of existing limited partners into the appropriate new feeder structure. The target effective date for the completion of the Reorganization is December 1, 2025. The precise sequencing and mechanics of the multi-step transaction will be developed and refined in the course of the engagement, in consultation with the Client and its other advisors.

**3.2 Scope of Legal Services**

Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement is limited to the following specific legal services in connection with the Reorganization:

> \(a\) **Tax Analysis Memoranda.** Preparation of comprehensive tax analysis memoranda addressing the U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Reorganization under, among other provisions, Internal Revenue Code (\"IRC\") §§ 721(a), 721(b), 723, 731(a), 731(c), 704(c), 752, 367(a), 367(b), 1446, and 897, and Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3. The tax analysis memoranda will address the characterization of each step of the multi-step Reorganization, including the contribution of assets by the offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the treatment of assumed or shifted liabilities, the application of the anti-mixing bowl rules, and the withholding tax implications for non-U.S. limited partners.
>
> \(b\) **Private Letter Ruling Request.** Drafting, revising, and finalizing a private letter ruling request (the \"PLR Request\") to be submitted to the Internal Revenue Service\'s Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\"), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The PLR Request will seek rulings on the specific tax consequences of the Reorganization that are identified in the course of the engagement as requiring advance IRS guidance for purposes of transaction certainty.
>
> \(c\) **Ancillary IRS Procedural Documents.** Preparation and filing of all ancillary IRS procedural documents required in connection with the PLR Request, including IRS Forms 2848 (Powers of Attorney and Declarations of Representative), penalties of perjury declarations, user fee transmittals, and pre-submission and supplemental correspondence with the IRS.
>
