matches.line: This Agreement of Limited Partnership (this **\"Agreement\"**) of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the **\"Partnership\"** or the **\"Fund\"**), is entered into as of the date of the First Close (as defined below) by and among Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as the general partner (the **\"General Partner\"** or **\"GP\"**), and each Person who is admitted as a limited partner of the Partnership (each, a **\"Limited Partner\"** or **\"LP\"** and, collectively, the **\"Limited Partners\"**), in each case in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth herein. The General Partner and the Limited Partners are sometimes referred to herein individually as a **\"Partner\"** and collectively as the **\"Partners.\"**

**WHEREAS**, each Limited Partner desires to make a capital commitment to the Partnership on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement and in the Subscription Agreement executed by such Limited Partner; and

**\"Blocker Entity\"** means HGF V blocker Corp., a Delaware C corporation formed for the benefit of certain tax-exempt or non-U.S. Limited Partners to mitigate UBTI or effectively connected income concerns, as the General Partner may determine to be appropriate in connection with the Fund\'s investment program.

**\"Bridge Financing\"** means any short-term Fund-level borrowing (whether under the Subscription Credit Facility or otherwise) used to fund Portfolio Investments or other Partnership obligations in advance of or in lieu of issuing Capital Calls, which borrowing shall not remain outstanding for more than one hundred eighty (180) consecutive days from the date of the applicable borrowing.

**\"Early Close discount\"** means the ten (10) basis point reduction in the Management Fee rate applicable to Limited Partners admitted to the Partnership at the First Close, as described in Section 7.1(c) of this Agreement (resulting in a Management Fee rate of 1.65% per annum on Capital Commitments during the Investment Period, in lieu of 1.75%).
**\"Final Close Deadline\"** means February 15, 2027, being eighteen (18) months after the target date of the First Close.

**\"First Close\"** means the initial closing of Capital Commitments to the Partnership, targeted for August 15, 2025, at which the General Partner shall have accepted Capital Commitments aggregating at least Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000) (or such lesser amount as the General Partner may determine in its sole discretion).

**\"Fiscal Year\"** means the calendar year commencing on January 1 and ending on December 31 of each year; *provided*, that the first Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall commence on the date of the First Close and shall end on December 31 of such calendar year, and the final Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall end on the date of the final distribution of all Partnership assets and cancellation of the Certificate of Limited Partnership.

**\"Investment Period\"** means the period commencing on the date of the Final Close and expiring on the fifth (5th) anniversary of the Final Close, unless earlier terminated or suspended in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement (including Section 5.7 and Article X).

**\"Large LP discount\"** means the additional five (5) basis point reduction in the Management Fee rate applicable to Limited Partners committing One Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$150,000,000) or more to the Partnership, as described in Section 7.1(c) of this Agreement (resulting in a cumulative Management Fee rate of 1.60% per annum during the Investment Period for a First Close Limited Partner committing \$150,000,000 or more).

**\"Subscription Agreement\"** means the subscription agreement and related documents executed by each Limited Partner in connection with such Limited Partner\'s commitment to the Partnership, in the form attached hereto as Exhibit D (or as otherwise prescribed by the General Partner), together with all exhibits, schedules, questionnaires, and certifications attached thereto.

**\"Subsequent Close\"** means any closing of Capital Commitments to the Partnership occurring after the First Close and on or prior to the Final Close Deadline, at which additional Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership and/or existing Limited Partners may increase their Capital Commitments, in accordance with Section 3.4 of this Agreement.

The Partnership has been formed as a limited partnership under and pursuant to the Act by the filing (or the contemplated filing on or prior to the date of the First Close) of a Certificate of Limited Partnership with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. The Certificate of Limited Partnership identifies Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC as the sole general partner of the Partnership. The registered office of the Partnership in the State of Delaware is located at 400 South Ashbury Asset Advisors, Suite 3000, Wilmington, Delaware 19801, in care of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, which serves as the registered agent of the Partnership for service of process in the State of Delaware. The General Partner shall cause such amendments to the Certificate of Limited Partnership and such other filings and recordings as may be required or appropriate under the Act and the laws of any other jurisdiction in which the Partnership conducts business.

The Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall be the calendar year, commencing on January 1 and ending on December 31 of each year; *provided*, that the first Fiscal Year shall commence on the date of the First Close and end on December 31 of such calendar year, and the last Fiscal Year shall end on the date upon which all assets of the Partnership have been distributed and the Certificate of Limited Partnership has been cancelled.

\(a\) Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of which is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, is hereby admitted as the sole general partner of the Partnership upon its execution of this Agreement. The General Partner shall serve as the sole general partner of the Partnership for the duration of the Fund Term, subject to the provisions of Sections 12.6 and 12.7.

\(a\) Each Limited Partner shall be admitted to the Partnership upon (i) the execution and delivery by such Limited Partner of a Subscription Agreement and the joinder or counterpart signature page to this Agreement, (ii) the acceptance of such Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment by the General Partner, and (iii) the occurrence of the applicable Closing (as defined below) at which such Limited Partner is admitted.
**[Section 3.3 --- First Close]{.underline}**

\(a\) The First Close of Capital Commitments to the Partnership is targeted to occur on August 15, 2025 (the **\"First Close\"**), at which time the General Partner shall accept Capital Commitments from one or more Limited Partners.

\(b\) The First Close shall not occur unless the aggregate Capital Commitments accepted at the First Close (including the GP Commitment) equal or exceed Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000); *provided*, that the General Partner may, in its sole discretion, waive or reduce such minimum and proceed with the First Close at a lower aggregate commitment level if the General Partner determines that doing so is in the best interests of the Partnership.

\(c\) Upon the occurrence of the First Close, the Partnership shall commence its operations and the General Partner shall be authorized to make Capital Calls and to begin the investment program described in Article V.

\(a\) Following the First Close, the General Partner may hold one or more Subsequent Closes at such times as the General Partner may determine, at which additional Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership and/or existing Limited Partners may increase their Capital Commitments. Subsequent Closes may occur on a rolling basis through the Final Close Deadline of February 15, 2027 (being eighteen (18) months after the target date of the First Close).

\(b\) Each Limited Partner admitted at a Subsequent Close shall be required to make a catch-up capital contribution equal to such Limited Partner\'s pro rata share of all Capital Calls that were funded by the existing Partners prior to such Subsequent Close, together with interest thereon at the rate of eight percent (8%) per annum, compounded annually, from the date of the First Close (or, in the case of Capital Calls funded after the First Close, from the respective funding dates thereof) through the date of such Subsequent Close. > \(d\) *Minimum Commitment.* The minimum capital commitment for each Limited Partner admitted to the Fund is Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000), subject to waiver by the General Partner in its sole discretion. The smallest commitment at the First Close is the Fifty Million Dollar (\$50,000,000) commitment of Velthorn Family Office LLC.

> \(e\) *Investment Strategy.* The Fund\'s investment strategy, as described in the PPM, is focused on North American mid-market and upper-mid-market leveraged buyout transactions in the industrials, business services, healthcare services, and technology-enabled services sectors, with target equity investment sizes ranging from Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000) to Two Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$250,000,000) per portfolio company. This investment strategy is consistent with private equity fund structures that are typically eligible for, and commonly rely upon, the Section 3(c)(7) exclusion from the definition of \"investment company\" under the 1940 Act. The Fund is not a \"hedge fund\" or other type of pooled investment vehicle that would raise separate or additional concerns under the 1940 Act.

We note that Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC is registered with the SEC as an investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended (the \"**Advisers Act**\") (SEC File No. 801-79223; CRD No. 298417), and serves as the investment adviser to the Fund pursuant to the terms of the LPA and the advisory arrangements described therein. The Sponsor\'s registration as an investment adviser is reflected in its current Form ADV, Part 1A and Part 2A (Brochure), as filed with the SEC and available through the Investment Adviser Public Disclosure database maintained by the SEC and FINRA.

> \(i\) The securities or \"blue sky\" laws of any state or territory of the United States, including the Uniform Securities Act, the Delaware Securities Act, the New York Martin Act, or any other state securities statute, rule, or regulation. > \(ii\) The laws of any foreign jurisdiction, including the Cayman Islands (with respect to the offshore parallel vehicle, Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP, a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership), Bermuda (with respect to any Investor domiciled or organized therein, including Edgecombe Insurance Group Ltd., a Bermuda-domiciled insurance company), or any other non-U.S. jurisdiction. We note that the offering and sale of interests in the Offshore Feeder may be subject to the securities laws and regulatory requirements of the Cayman Islands and other foreign jurisdictions, and separate legal opinions from local counsel should be obtained with respect thereto;

> \(iii\) ERISA, the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, or any rules or regulations promulgated thereunder, including without limitation matters relating to (A) the characterization of the Fund\'s assets as \"plan assets\" under Section 3(42) of ERISA and the U.S. Department of Labor\'s Plan Asset Regulation (29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101, as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA), (B) unrelated business taxable income (\"**UBTI**\") under Sections 511 through 514 of the Code, (C) effectively connected income (\"**ECI**\") under Section 864 of the Code, (D) the Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act of 1980 (\"**FIRPTA**\") under Sections 897 and 1445 of the Code, or (E) the application of Section 1061 of the Code to carried interest allocations. **[Section 1 --- Notice of Distribution]{.underline}**

Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC (the **\"General Partner\"**), in its capacity as general partner of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP (the **\"Fund\"** or the **\"Partnership\"**), hereby gives notice, pursuant to Section \[**\] of the Partnership Agreement, that a distribution will be made to the Limited Partners of the Partnership on the date specified below. This Distribution Notice is being delivered to each Limited Partner in accordance with the notice provisions set forth in Section \[**\] of the Partnership Agreement.

The distribution described herein is being made in accordance with the European-style (whole-fund) distribution waterfall set forth in Article \[\_\_\] of the Partnership Agreement. As the Limited Partners are aware, under the European-style waterfall structure, distributions are calculated on a cumulative, whole-fund basis rather than on a deal-by-deal basis, such that the General Partner is not entitled to receive Carried Interest until all Capital Contributions (including those attributable to Management Fees, Organizational Expenses, and Fund Expenses) have been returned to the Partners and the Preferred Return has been paid in full on all such Capital Contributions.
**Distribution Date:** \[**\_\_\], 20\[**\]

The Record Date is the date as of which the identity and Sharing Percentages of the Limited Partners shall be determined for purposes of this distribution. Only those persons who are admitted as Limited Partners of the Partnership as of the Record Date, and whose interests have not been transferred, assigned, or withdrawn as of such date, shall be entitled to receive their proportionate share of the distribution described herein.
**[Section 2 --- Aggregate Distribution Amount]{.underline}**
The total aggregate amount to be distributed to all Partners of the Partnership pursuant to this Distribution Notice is:
The source of this distribution is as follows (each applicable source is indicated):

The aggregate distribution amount set forth above represents the net amount available for distribution to the Partners after giving effect to: (i) all Fund-level expenses (including Management Fees, Organizational Expenses, and other Fund Expenses) accrued or payable as of the date hereof; (ii) amounts applied to the repayment (whether mandatory or voluntary) of outstanding borrowings under the subscription credit facility maintained by the Partnership with Ashford National Bank, N.A., including any accrued interest, fees, and other amounts due and payable thereunder; (iii) reserves established or maintained by the General Partner in its reasonable discretion in accordance with Section \[\_\_\] of the Partnership Agreement, as further described in Section 7 of this Distribution Notice; and (iv) applicable withholding taxes, including U.S. federal, state, and local withholding taxes imposed on distributions to non-U.S. Limited Partners as further described in Section 5 below.

The General Partner has determined, in its reasonable judgment and in consultation with the Fund\'s independent auditors and legal counsel, that the foregoing amount is available for distribution in accordance with the terms of the Partnership Agreement and the Fund\'s organizational documents, and that such distribution will not impair the ability of the Partnership to satisfy its known or reasonably anticipated obligations, liabilities, and commitments.

The distribution described in this Distribution Notice is allocated among the following tiers of the European-style whole-fund distribution waterfall, as set forth in Section \[\_\_\] of the Partnership Agreement. The allocation set forth below reflects the cumulative status of all distributions made by the Partnership to date, including the distribution contemplated by this Distribution Notice. For the avoidance of doubt, the waterfall allocation is calculated on a cumulative, whole-fund basis, taking into account all prior Capital Contributions, all prior distributions, and all accrued but unpaid Preferred Return.

Amounts allocated to Tier 1 represent the return to each Partner of an amount equal to such Partner\'s aggregate Capital Contributions (including Capital Contributions made by such Partner that were applied by the Partnership to pay Management Fees, Organizational Expenses, and Fund Expenses), to the extent such Capital Contributions have not been previously returned through prior distributions. Distributions under this Tier 1 are allocated among the Partners in proportion to their respective unreturned Capital Contributions.

**Note to Limited Partners:** Amounts distributed under this Tier 1 constitute a return of capital and are not treated as income or gain to the Limited Partners for purposes of the Partnership Agreement waterfall. The federal income tax characterization of such amounts may differ from the waterfall characterization and will be reflected on each Limited Partner\'s Schedule K-1 for the applicable fiscal year, as further described in Section 5 of this Distribution Notice.

Amounts allocated to Tier 2 represent the payment to each Partner of the Preferred Return, being a cumulative, compounded return at the rate of eight percent (8%) per annum on such Partner\'s unreturned Capital Contributions, to the extent the Preferred Return has not been previously distributed. The Preferred Return accrues from the date on which each Capital Contribution is funded by such Partner and is computed on the basis of unreturned capital (i.e., Capital Contributions reduced by prior Tier 1 distributions attributable thereto). The Preferred Return is compounded annually on each December 31 (the fiscal year end of the Partnership) and on the date of each distribution. Distributions under this Tier 2 are allocated among the Partners in proportion to their respective accrued and unpaid Preferred Return.

**Note to Limited Partners:** The Preferred Return is calculated on an aggregate, whole-fund basis, taking into account all Capital Contributions made by each Partner over the life of the Fund and all prior distributions of Preferred Return. The General Partner has computed the Preferred Return in accordance with the methodology set forth in the Partnership Agreement, and such calculation has been reviewed by Pinnacle Fund Services LLC, the Fund Administrator.

Amounts allocated to Tier 3 represent the \"catch-up\" allocation designed to bring the General Partner\'s cumulative share of net profits to twenty percent (20%) of all cumulative net profits distributed by the Partnership. Distributions under Tier 3 are allocated eighty percent (80%) to the General Partner (and through the General Partner to Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, as its sole member) and twenty percent (20%) to the Limited Partners (pro rata based on their respective Sharing Percentages), until the General Partner has received, on a cumulative basis, aggregate distributions equal to twenty percent (20%) of all cumulative net profits (defined as the sum of cumulative Tier 2, Tier 3, and Tier 4 distributions).

**Note to Limited Partners:** The 80/20 catch-up allocation structure ensures that, once the eight percent (8%) Preferred Return has been fully satisfied, the General Partner receives its twenty percent (20%) Carried Interest on all cumulative profits of the Partnership. The catch-up is calculated on a whole-fund basis, taking into account all prior Tier 2, Tier 3, and Tier 4 distributions. If the catch-up has been fully satisfied by prior distributions, no further amounts will be allocated to this Tier 3.

Amounts allocated to Tier 4 represent the residual profit-sharing allocation after the Preferred Return has been paid in full and the GP Catch-Up has been fully satisfied. Distributions under Tier 4 are allocated eighty percent (80%) to the Limited Partners (pro rata based on their respective Sharing Percentages) and twenty percent (20%) to the General Partner as Carried Interest.

**Note to Limited Partners:** Distributions in this Tier 4 represent the standard profit-sharing ratio applicable to the Fund after the Preferred Return hurdle has been cleared and the General Partner has been brought to its full twenty percent (20%) participation in cumulative net profits through the Tier 3 catch-up mechanism. Carried Interest distributions to the General Partner remain subject to the clawback obligation described in Section 8 of this Distribution Notice and Section \[\_\_\] of the Partnership Agreement.

Each Limited Partner\'s individual share of the distribution described in this Distribution Notice is set forth on **Schedule A** attached hereto. The allocation to each Limited Partner reflects such Partner\'s pro rata Sharing Percentage (as defined in the Partnership Agreement) and the waterfall allocation described in Section 3 above.

Limited Partners are further reminded that amounts characterized as Carried Interest (whether allocated under Tier 3 or Tier 4 of the waterfall) are subject to Section 1061 of the Code, which was enacted as part of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 and imposes a **three-year holding period requirement** for long-term capital gain treatment on net capital gains with respect to \"applicable partnership interests\" (as defined in Section 1061(c) of the Code). Under Section 1061, net capital gains allocable to applicable partnership interests that would otherwise be treated as long-term capital gain but for which the underlying assets have been held for three years or less are recharacterized as short-term capital gain. The General Partner will provide relevant information regarding the application of Section 1061 on the Schedule K-1s issued to the Partners.

Dear Dr. Yeung and Ms. Dasgupta:

Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm the terms of our engagement to serve as fund counsel to Cobalt Ventures LP in connection with the matters described below. This engagement letter (this \"Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions under which Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") will provide legal services to Cobalt Ventures LP (\"Cobalt\" or the \"Client\").

**[1. Purpose and Introduction]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm its engagement by Cobalt Ventures LP to serve as fund counsel in connection with the structuring, formation, and fund-raising for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP (the \"Fund\" or \"CLSO Fund I\"), a proposed Delaware limited partnership. We understand that the Fund will be Cobalt\'s inaugural dedicated opportunistic life-sciences investment vehicle, and that Cobalt is targeting aggregate committed capital of Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000), with a hard cap of One Billion Dollars (\$1,000,000,000).

By way of background, Cobalt is a California-headquartered venture capital sponsor focused on the biotechnology and life-sciences sectors. Founded in 2018 by Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta, Cobalt currently manages approximately \$420 million in assets under management across two prior vintage vehicles --- Cobalt Ventures Fund A, LP (vintage 2019) and Cobalt Ventures Fund B, LP (vintage 2022). The launch of CLSO Fund I represents a significant strategic milestone for the Cobalt platform, expanding the firm\'s investment mandate into opportunistic life-sciences investments across stage, geography, and modality.

This Letter sets forth the terms under which Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services in connection with the structuring, formation, and fund-raising of the Fund and related entities, and it supersedes any prior oral or written understandings between the parties regarding the scope and terms of this engagement.

**3.1 Fund Structuring and Entity Formation**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise the Client on the optimal legal and organizational structure for the Fund and will be responsible for the formation of each Fund Entity. This workstream will include the following:

> \(a\) **Structural Analysis.** Analysis of fund structure alternatives, including a single-tier Delaware limited partnership, parallel fund structures (including for non-U.S. investors or investors requiring a separately managed account), blocker corporation arrangements, alternative investment vehicle (\"AIV\") structures, and master-feeder options. Our analysis will take into account the anticipated investor base, the Client\'s investment strategy, tax efficiency, regulatory considerations, and administrative complexity.
>
> \(b\) **Fund Structuring Memorandum.** Preparation and delivery of a comprehensive Fund Structuring Memorandum setting forth Calderwood & Harkness\'s analysis and recommendations regarding the recommended fund architecture, including a diagram of the proposed entity structure, a summary of the principal advantages and disadvantages of each structural alternative considered, and our recommended approach. The target delivery date for the Fund Structuring Memorandum is **April 30, 2026**.
>
> \(c\) **Delaware Formation Filings.** Preparation and filing of the Certificate of Limited Partnership for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP, and the Certificates of Formation for Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC and Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC, with the Delaware Division of Corporations. If the blocker corporation is determined to be necessary, Calderwood & Harkness will also prepare and file the Certificate of Incorporation for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I (Blocker), Inc.
>
> \(d\) **EIN Applications.** Preparation and submission of IRS Form SS-4 (Application for Employer Identification Number) for CLSO Fund I, CLSO GP I, and CLSO Management I.
>
> \(e\) **Registered Agent Coordination.** Coordination with Hollowell Technologies, the Client\'s designated registered agent in Delaware, to ensure that each Fund Entity is properly set up for service of process and annual compliance filings.

**3.2 Tax Structuring**

The target delivery date for the Tax Structuring Memorandum is **April 30, 2026**.

The first draft of the LPA is targeted for delivery on or about **May 31, 2026**. The LPA will address, among other things, the following key economic and governance terms:
>
> *Economic Terms:*
>
> • Management Fee: 2.00% per annum of committed capital during the investment period, stepping down to 2.00% of invested capital (or net invested capital, as determined) thereafter;
>
> • Carried Interest: 20% of net profits, subject to the preferred return and GP catch-up described below;
>
> • Preferred Return: 8% per annum, compounded annually;
>
> • GP Catch-up: 100% of distributions after the preferred return has been achieved, until the general partner has received 20% of cumulative net profits;
>
> • Carry Escrow: 30% of carried interest distributions to be held in escrow pending final liquidation of the Fund to secure the general partner\'s clawback obligation;
>
> • Clawback: Standard general partner clawback obligation, net of taxes, to be triggered upon final liquidation of the Fund to the extent the general partner has received carried interest distributions in excess of amounts to which it is entitled on a cumulative basis;
>
> • Recycling Allowance: 15% of aggregate committed capital may be recycled (i.e., proceeds from realized investments may be recalled for reinvestment during the investment period);
>
> • Concentration Limit: No more than 15% of aggregate committed capital may be invested in any single portfolio company, measured at the time of investment;
>
> • Organizational Expense Cap: Organizational expenses in excess of \$1,500,000 shall be borne by the general partner or the management company;
>
> • Broken-Deal Expense Cap: Broken-deal expenses in excess of \$500,000 per unconsummated transaction shall be borne by the general partner or the management company.

> *Governance Provisions:*

> • Key Person Event provisions, identifying Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta as key persons, with suspension of the investment period upon a key person event and reinstatement mechanics;

> • Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") provisions, including composition, authority, and procedures for the resolution of conflicts of interest;
>
> • Removal rights, including removal of the general partner for cause and no-fault removal by a supermajority in interest of the limited partners;
>
> • Default provisions, including the consequences of a limited partner\'s failure to fund a capital call;
>
> • Excuse and exclusion provisions, permitting limited partners to be excused or excluded from particular investments under specified circumstances (e.g., legal, regulatory, or tax impediments).

> *Regulatory Provisions:*

**ARDENT CAPITAL GP III LLC** 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, NY 10022

Registered Agent: Prestige Registered Agents LLC 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201 Dover, DE 19904

February 5, 2024

VIA ELECTRONIC DELIVERY AND OVERNIGHT COURIER

Mr. Thomas Engström Chief Investment Officer Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System Commitment: \$225,000,000

Ms. Annika Johansson Director of Private Equity Crestwood Endowment Partners Commitment: \$150,000,000

Mr. Derek Mallinson Head of Alternatives Pinnacle Insurance Group Commitment: \$175,000,000

Ms. Catherine Whitfield Managing Director Graystone Family Office LLC Commitment: \$50,000,000

**Re:** Ardent Capital Partners III LP --- Notification of Proposed Management Company Restructuring, Economics Realignment, and Departures of Senior Principals; Solicitation of LPAC Consent Pursuant to Section 9.4 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership

Dear Members of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee:

**[1. Introduction and Purpose]{.underline}**

Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"**General Partner**\"), as the sole general partner of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"**Fund**\" or \"**Fund III**\"), is writing to provide notification of, and to solicit the consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\" or the \"**Committee**\") to, a proposed restructuring of the management company and related realignment of economics among the Fund\'s principals (the \"**Restructuring**\"). This letter sets forth the material terms and circumstances of the Restructuring in detail, together with the background and rationale therefor, and identifies the specific consents being requested of the LPAC in connection therewith.

The consent of the LPAC is being solicited pursuant to **Section 9.4** of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund, dated as of April 15, 2019 (as amended, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"**LPA**\"), which requires LPAC consent for certain material structural changes to the General Partner, the management company, or the economic arrangements among the principals, including without limitation any change in the ownership or control of the General Partner, any material amendment to the organizational documents of the General Partner, and any material realignment of the carried interest or management fee economics of the Fund.

The General Partner respectfully requests that each LPAC member review this letter and the enclosed materials carefully and execute and return the enclosed Form of Written Consent (the \"**Consent**\") at or prior to the LPAC meeting scheduled for **February 14, 2024**, which will be held virtually via videoconference. Details regarding the videoconference will be provided under separate cover. LPAC members may deliver their consent either by execution and return of the enclosed Consent in advance of the meeting or by affirmative vote at the meeting itself.

In connection with the Restructuring, the General Partner has engaged **Calderwood & Harkness LLP** (Nicholas Stern, responsible partner, and Owen Fischer, lead associate) as restructuring counsel to advise the General Partner on the structural, governance, and transactional aspects of the Restructuring. **Pemberton Hale LLP** (Victoria Langford, responsible partner) continues to serve as fund counsel for routine Fund operations and has provided guidance on LPA interpretation and side-letter compliance matters. The General Partner wishes to note that Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Pemberton Hale LLP represent the General Partner and the Fund, respectively, and do not represent any individual limited partner or the LPAC. LPAC members are encouraged to consult with their own legal and tax advisors as they deem appropriate.

**[2. Background on the Fund]{.underline}**

Ardent Capital Partners III LP is a Delaware limited partnership formed in 2019 for the purpose of making control-oriented equity investments in middle-market industrial and business-services companies, primarily in North America. The Fund targets companies with enterprise values between \$150 million and \$750 million, with a focus on sectors where the principals of Ardent Capital have deep operational expertise and established proprietary sourcing channels, including industrial technology, specialty distribution, environmental services, and facility management.

As of the date of this letter, the key parameters of the Fund are as follows:

**Total Commitments.** The Fund has aggregate capital commitments of **\$2.8 billion** from **47 limited partners**, including leading public pension systems, endowments and foundations, insurance companies, family offices, and other institutional investors.

**Capital Called and Invested.** As of the date of this letter, the Fund has called approximately **\$1.96 billion** in capital from its limited partners, representing approximately **70%** of total commitments. Of the capital called, approximately **\$1.88 billion** has been invested or is reserved for follow-on investments across the Fund\'s portfolio, with the remainder having been applied to management fees, organizational expenses, and other fund-level charges.

**Portfolio Overview.** The Fund currently holds **11 active portfolio companies** across the industrial and business-services sectors. Each portfolio company is actively managed by a dedicated deal team within Ardent Capital, and in each case Ardent Capital holds board representation and exercises significant operational influence.

**Fund Performance.** As of September 30, 2023, the most recent quarterly valuation date, the Fund\'s aggregate performance was as follows:

> • Gross multiple of invested capital (\"**MOIC**\"): **1.42x**
>
> • Net internal rate of return (\"**IRR**\"): **14.7%**
>
> • Total unrealized value: approximately **\$2.33 billion** (based on fair market valuations prepared by Broadleaf Consulting Group, the Fund\'s independent valuation advisor, and reviewed by Heathrow Whitman & Co., the Fund\'s auditor)
>
> • Total realized proceeds: approximately **\$445 million** (reflecting partial realizations and dividend recapitalizations from three portfolio companies)

**GP Commitment.** The General Partner and its principals have made an aggregate capital commitment to the Fund of **\$42 million**, representing **1.5%** of total Fund commitments, which is consistent with the minimum GP commitment described in the Fund\'s confidential private placement memorandum dated March 2019.

**Investment Period.** The investment period of the Fund commenced on June 30, 2019, and is scheduled to end on **June 30, 2025**. As of the date of this letter, the Fund has approximately \$840 million of uncalled capital commitments available for new investments during the remaining portion of the investment period.

**Fund Term.** The term of the Fund is scheduled to expire on **December 31, 2029**, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the General Partner in accordance with Section 12.1 of the LPA.

**Management Fee.** The Fund pays an annual management fee equal to **1.75%** of aggregate capital commitments during the investment period (approximately **\$49 million** per year at current commitment levels) and **1.50%** of invested capital (net of write-downs and write-offs) following the expiration of the investment period. The management fee is payable quarterly in advance to Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"**Management Company**\" or \"**ManCo**\"), the Fund\'s SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD #298417).

**Carried Interest.** The General Partner is entitled to receive carried interest equal to **20%** of the Fund\'s net profits (calculated on a whole-Fund basis), subject to an **8% per annum preferred return** to the limited partners and a **100% catch-up** to the General Partner thereafter, in each case as more fully described in Section 6.2 of the LPA.

**Current Principals.** As of the date of this letter, the principals of the General Partner are:

> • **Marcus Aldridge** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
>
> • **Priya Narayanan** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
>
> • **David Kellner** --- Senior Partner
>
> • **Joanna Trask** --- Partner
>
> • **Robert Hsiao** --- Partner

**[3. Summary of Proposed Restructuring]{.underline}**

**3.1 Overview.** The Restructuring involves four principal workstreams, each of which is described in detail below:

> 1\. **Entity Restructuring** --- the formation of new holding entities and the reorganization of the ownership structure of the General Partner and the Management Company;
>
> 2\. **Economics Realignment** --- the reallocation of carried interest and Management Company profit-share economics among the remaining and next-generation principals;
>
> 3\. **Departing Principal Separation** --- the orderly departure and separation of two senior principals, David Kellner and Joanna Trask, and the negotiation and execution of their respective separation and release agreements; and
>
> 4\. **LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance** --- the solicitation of LPAC consent as required under the LPA and compliance with notification and consent provisions contained in individual side letters.

The principal rationale for the Restructuring is fourfold: (a) to implement a thoughtful succession plan that positions Ardent Capital for long-term stability and continuity across multiple fund cycles; (b) to enhance governance by establishing a consolidated holding company structure with clear lines of authority and accountability; (c) to integrate the next generation of talent --- specifically, Elena Marchetti and Samuel Okonkwo, each of whom has made significant contributions to the Fund\'s investment activities and portfolio management --- into the economic and governance framework of Ardent Capital; and (d) to facilitate the orderly transition of responsibilities and economics following the planned departure of David Kellner (who is retiring after a distinguished career) and the voluntary departure of Joanna Trask. The General Partner believes that the Restructuring will strengthen Ardent Capital\'s institutional platform and is in the best interests of the Fund and its limited partners.

**3.2 Entity Restructuring**

The structural component of the Restructuring involves the formation of two new Delaware limited liability companies and the reorganization of the ownership structure of the General Partner and the Management Company. Specifically:

**Formation of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC.** A new Delaware limited liability company, **Ardent Capital Holdings LLC** (\"**HoldCo**\"), will be formed to serve as the parent holding company of both the Management Company and the General Partner (through an intermediate entity). HoldCo will be governed by an amended and restated limited liability company agreement that provides for the rights, obligations, and economic entitlements of its members.

**Formation of Ardent GP Intermediate LLC.** A new Delaware limited liability company, **Ardent GP Intermediate LLC** (\"**GP Intermediate**\"), will be formed to serve as an intermediate holding entity between HoldCo and the General Partner. GP Intermediate will be a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo.

**Post-Restructuring Organizational Structure.** Upon completion of the Restructuring, the organizational structure will be as follows:

> • HoldCo will be the **sole member** of both (i) the Management Company (Ardent Capital Management LLC, SEC-registered investment adviser, CRD #298417) and (ii) GP Intermediate.
>
> • GP Intermediate will be the **sole member** of the General Partner (Ardent Capital GP III LLC).
>
> • The General Partner will continue to serve as the sole general partner of the Fund.

**Current Structure Being Replaced.** Under the current organizational structure, the five individual principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) hold direct membership interests in both the General Partner and the Management Company. The direct-ownership model was adopted at the time of the Fund\'s formation for simplicity, but as Ardent Capital has grown and matured as an institution, the General Partner has determined that a consolidated holding company structure is more appropriate and consistent with industry best practices for institutional-quality private equity platforms. The holding company structure also facilitates the admission and withdrawal of individual principals without requiring amendments to the organizational documents of the General Partner or the Management Company, thereby reducing administrative burden and the need for LP consents in connection with future personnel changes (to the extent otherwise permitted under the LPA).

**HoldCo Membership.** Following the Restructuring, the members of HoldCo will be:

> • **Marcus Aldridge** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
>
> • **Priya Narayanan** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
>
> • **Robert Hsiao** --- Partner
>
> • **Elena Marchetti** --- Principal
>
> • **Samuel Okonkwo** --- Principal

The **Managing Members** of HoldCo will be Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan, who will have the authority to manage the business and affairs of HoldCo (and, through HoldCo, the Management Company and the General Partner) in accordance with the terms of the HoldCo operating agreement.

**3.3 Principal Departures**

**David Kellner --- Retirement.** David Kellner, a Senior Partner of Ardent Capital and one of the founding members of the Fund III team, has informed the General Partner of his intention to retire from active investment management. Mr. Kellner, age 61, has had a distinguished 35-year career in private equity and has been instrumental in building Ardent Capital\'s industrial services franchise. His retirement will be effective **March 31, 2024**, following a transition period during which he will work with the remaining principals to ensure an orderly handover of his portfolio company board responsibilities and deal-team oversight functions. Following his retirement, Mr. Kellner will transition to a **Senior Advisor** role for a two-year advisory term (April 1, 2024 through March 31, 2026), during which he will be available for consultation on portfolio matters at an annual advisory fee of **\$350,000** per year.

The key economic terms of Mr. Kellner\'s departure are as follows:

> • **Current GP Interest:** Mr. Kellner currently holds a **15%** membership interest in the General Partner and is entitled to a **15%** share of the Fund\'s carried interest.
>
> • **Carried Interest Retention:** Mr. Kellner will retain **100%** of his vested carried interest in Fund III, which, based on the September 30, 2023 valuation, represents an accrued carried interest of approximately **\$13,140,000**. Such retained carried interest will be subject to a modified clawback obligation that will continue for a period of **three (3) years** following Mr. Kellner\'s retirement date (i.e., through March 31, 2027), at which time his clawback exposure will expire.
>
> • **Management Company Economics:** Mr. Kellner\'s share of ManCo profit distributions will cease effective as of his retirement date. He will receive no further profit-share or other economic distributions from the Management Company after March 31, 2024.
>
> • **Restrictive Covenants:** Mr. Kellner has agreed to a **non-competition** covenant for a period of **18 months** following his retirement date and **non-solicitation** covenants with respect to both employees and limited partners of Ardent Capital for a period of **24 months** each following his retirement date.

**Joanna Trask --- Voluntary Departure.** Joanna Trask, a Partner of Ardent Capital, has informed the General Partner of her decision to depart from Ardent Capital voluntarily to pursue a senior role at another investment firm. Ms. Trask, age 48, has been a valued member of the Ardent Capital team and has led several successful investments in the business-services sector during her tenure. Her departure will be effective **April 15, 2024**, following a transition period during which she will complete the handover of her responsibilities.

The key economic terms of Ms. Trask\'s departure are as follows:

> • **Current GP Interest:** Ms. Trask currently holds a **12%** membership interest in the General Partner and is entitled to a **12%** share of the Fund\'s carried interest.
>
> • **Carried Interest Retention:** Ms. Trask will retain **60%** of her vested carried interest in Fund III, representing approximately **\$6,307,200** based on the September 30, 2023 valuation. The remaining **40%** of her vested carried interest, representing approximately **\$4,204,800**, will be forfeited. In addition, Ms. Trask will forfeit **100%** of any unvested carried interest. Her retained carried interest will be subject to a clawback obligation for a period of **two (2) years** following her departure date (i.e., through April 15, 2026).
>
> • **Separation Payment:** Ms. Trask will receive a one-time lump-sum separation payment of **\$1,250,000**, payable within 30 days following her departure date, in consideration of her execution of a general release of claims and compliance with her ongoing restrictive covenants.
>
> • **Restrictive Covenants:** Ms. Trask has agreed to a **non-competition** covenant for a period of **12 months** following her departure date and **non-solicitation** covenants with respect to employees and limited partners of Ardent Capital for a period of **18 months** each following her departure date.

Both departures are subject to the terms of negotiated separation and release agreements (each, a \"**Separation Agreement**\") that are currently being finalized. Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask are each independently represented by **Whitford & Chase LLP** (Richard Beaulieu, partner) in connection with the negotiation of their respective Separation Agreements. Copies of the Separation Agreements (in substantially final form) will be made available to LPAC members upon request, subject to applicable confidentiality provisions.

**3.4 Economics Realignment**

Upon the effective dates of the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, the aggregate **27%** carried interest share held by the departing principals (representing Mr. Kellner\'s 15% plus Ms. Trask\'s 12%) will be redistributed among the remaining and next-generation principals. The proposed post-Restructuring allocation of carried interest is set forth in the following table:

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**     **Pre-Restructuring Carry Share**   **Post-Restructuring Carry Share**   **Change**
  ----------------- ----------------------------------- ------------------------------------ -----------------
  Marcus Aldridge   35%                                 42%                                  +7%

  Priya Narayanan   30%                                 36%                                  +6%

  Robert Hsiao      8%                                  14%                                  +6%

  Elena Marchetti   0%                                  4%                                   +4%

  Samuel Okonkwo    0%                                  4%                                   +4%

  **Total**         **100%**                            **100%**                             **---**
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The same percentage allocations reflected in the table above will apply to Management Company Profit Share distributions. For reference, Management Company Profit Share distributions (representing approximately 35% of annual management fee revenue retained by the Management Company after deduction of operating expenses) have averaged approximately **\$17,150,000 per year** over the life of the Fund to date. The economics realignment does not alter the overall quantum of management fees or carried interest payable by the Fund or its limited partners; rather, it reflects solely the internal allocation of such economics among the principals of the General Partner and the Management Company.

The following fundamental economic terms of the Fund remain **unchanged** by the Restructuring:

> • The carried interest rate remains at **20%** of net profits;
>
> • The preferred return remains at **8%** per annum;
>
> • The catch-up remains at **100%** to the General Partner;
>
> • The clawback structure remains unchanged, including **100% joint and several liability** of the General Partner and its principals, with a **30% individual escrow** of carried interest distributions (the \"**Escrow**\"); and
>
> • The mechanics of carried interest calculation (whole-Fund, European-style waterfall) remain unchanged.

With respect to **accrued carried interest**, as of September 30, 2023, the Fund\'s total accrued (but undistributed) carried interest was approximately **\$87,600,000**. The vested and retained portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s accrued carried interest will be carved out and preserved in accordance with the terms of their respective Separation Agreements, as described in Section 3.3 above. The redistribution set forth in the table above applies on a **go-forward basis** to carried interest attributable to future appreciation in the Fund\'s portfolio from and after the effective date of the Restructuring. The specific mechanics of the transition and allocation of accrued versus go-forward carry will be set forth in the amended carry allocation provisions of the GP\'s organizational documents and in Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.

**3.5 GP Commitment Reallocation**

The total GP commitment to the Fund is **\$42,000,000**. As a result of the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, their combined unfunded GP commitment of **\$3,402,000** (consisting of \$1,890,000 attributable to Mr. Kellner and \$1,512,000 attributable to Ms. Trask) must be assumed by the remaining principals to ensure that the GP commitment is fully funded through the remainder of the investment period and the balance of the Fund\'s term. The funded portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s GP commitments will remain in the Fund and will be treated in accordance with their respective Separation Agreements and the LPA.

The unfunded portion of the departing principals\' GP commitment will be assumed by the remaining HoldCo members on a pro rata basis, consistent with their post-Restructuring percentage interests, as follows:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **Post-Restructuring %**   **Assumed Unfunded GP Commitment**
  ----------------------- -------------------------- ------------------------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         42%                        \$1,428,840

  Priya Narayanan         36%                        \$1,224,720

  Robert Hsiao            14%                        \$476,280

  Elena Marchetti         4%                         \$136,080

  Samuel Okonkwo          4%                         \$136,080

  **Total**               **100%**                   **\$3,402,000**
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each remaining principal has confirmed his or her willingness and ability to fund the assumed unfunded GP commitment in accordance with the Fund\'s capital call schedule. The General Partner has received written commitments from each of the above-named individuals to this effect.

**[4. Key-Person Analysis]{.underline}**

Section 5.2 of the LPA designates **Marcus Aldridge** and **Priya Narayanan** as \"Key Persons\" of the Fund. Under Section 5.2, a \"Key Person Event\" is triggered if: (a) both Key Persons cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, or (b) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund and a replacement Key Person is not approved by the LPAC within 120 calendar days of such cessation.

The General Partner confirms that **neither David Kellner nor Joanna Trask is a designated Key Person** under Section 5.2 of the LPA. Accordingly, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask **do not trigger a Key Person Event** under the LPA, and the investment period will continue without suspension or interruption.

Both Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan will continue to serve as Co-Founders and Managing Partners of Ardent Capital and will continue to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, consistent with their obligations under the LPA. Neither Mr. Aldridge nor Ms. Narayanan has any present intention to reduce his or her involvement with the Fund or to pursue other business activities that would be inconsistent with the Key Person requirements of Section 5.2.

**Expanded Key-Person Provisions in Side Letters.** In connection with its side-letter compliance review, the General Partner and its counsel have identified that **6 of the 14** side letters currently in effect contain \"expanded key person\" provisions that designate David Kellner as a \"Contributing Person\" or use analogous terminology. These provisions generally require that the General Partner provide the applicable limited partner with written notice within **15 business days** of any Contributing Person\'s departure from active involvement with the Fund. The General Partner will comply with all such notification requirements in a timely manner.

Additionally, the General Partner has identified that **3 of the 6** side letters containing expanded key-person provisions grant the applicable limited partner a right to request a **90-day suspension** of the investment period pending LPAC review in the event of a Contributing Person\'s departure. The General Partner does not believe that such a suspension is warranted in light of (i) the continued full-time involvement of both designated Key Persons (Aldridge and Narayanan), (ii) the orderly nature of Mr. Kellner\'s planned retirement and transition to a Senior Advisor role, (iii) the depth and continuity of the remaining investment team, and (iv) the ongoing strong performance of the Fund\'s portfolio. The General Partner intends to engage directly and proactively with each of the applicable limited partners to discuss these matters and to address any questions or concerns.

**[5. Side-Letter Compliance Summary]{.underline}**

The Fund has **14 side letters** currently in effect with various limited partners. In connection with the Restructuring, the General Partner and its counsel at Pemberton Hale LLP and Calderwood & Harkness LLP have conducted a comprehensive review of all 14 side letters to assess compliance with the terms thereof in light of the proposed Restructuring. The results of that review are summarized below:

**Most Favored Nation (\"MFN\") Provisions.** Eleven (11) of the 14 side letters contain MFN provisions requiring the General Partner to notify the applicable limited partner of, and/or extend to the applicable limited partner, any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner. The General Partner has determined that the Restructuring does not involve the granting of any more favorable terms to any limited partner and, accordingly, no MFN issues have been identified.

**Fee discount or Rebate Provisions.** Eight (8) of the 14 side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner a fee discount, management fee rebate, or other fee accommodation. The Restructuring does not alter the management fee rates of the Fund (which remain at 1.75% of committed capital during the investment period and 1.50% of invested capital thereafter), and accordingly, no impact on fee-related side-letter provisions has been identified.

**Co-Investment Priority Rights.** Nine (9) of the 14 side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner co-investment priority rights or preferential co-investment allocation rights. The General Partner intends to update its internal co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal allocations and team responsibilities resulting from the Restructuring. The fundamental co-investment allocation framework --- which is based on commitment size, co-investment track record, and ability to respond to allocation opportunities within the required timeframe --- will remain substantively unchanged. LPAC members with co-investment priority rights will continue to receive advance notice of co-investment opportunities in accordance with their respective side letters.

**Material Change Notification and Consent Provisions.** Four (4) side letters --- those with **Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System**, **Pinnacle Insurance Group**, **Crestwood Endowment Partners**, and **Haverford Capital Partners** --- contain provisions requiring prior written notice and, in certain cases, affirmative consent to any \"material change in the management structure\" of the General Partner, the Management Company, or the Fund\'s investment team. This letter and the LPAC consent process described herein serve as the required notification to the three LPAC members (Ridgeline, Pinnacle, and Crestwood) that hold such provisions. Separate notice will be provided to Haverford Capital Partners in accordance with the specific requirements of its side letter.

A detailed **Side-Letter Compliance and Key-Person Analysis Memorandum** is currently being finalized by Pemberton Hale LLP and Calderwood & Harkness LLP. This memorandum, which will include a provision-by-provision analysis of each side letter and a comprehensive key-person analysis, will be made available to LPAC members upon request. LPAC members who wish to receive a copy of the memorandum should contact Nicholas Stern at Calderwood & Harkness LLP or Victoria Langford at Pemberton Hale LLP.

**[6. Impact on Fund Operations]{.underline}**

The General Partner wishes to assure the LPAC that the Restructuring has been designed to ensure continuity and stability in the Fund\'s operations and to minimize any disruption to the Fund\'s investment activities and portfolio management. Specifically, the General Partner confirms that the Restructuring will have **no impact** on the following:

> • **Investment Strategy:** The Fund\'s investment strategy --- control-oriented equity investments in middle-market industrial and business-services companies --- will remain unchanged. The Fund will continue to pursue its stated investment objectives in accordance with the investment guidelines and restrictions set forth in the LPA and the Fund\'s confidential private placement memorandum.
>
> • **Investment Period:** The investment period of the Fund will continue through its scheduled expiration on **June 30, 2025**, without suspension, acceleration, or modification of any kind.
>
> • **Management Fee Rates:** The management fee rates of the Fund will remain unchanged at **1.75%** of committed capital during the investment period and **1.50%** of invested capital following the expiration of the investment period.
>
> • **Carried Interest Terms:** The carried interest rate of **20%** of net profits, the **8%** preferred return, the **100%** catch-up, and all other terms of the carried interest waterfall and clawback provisions of the LPA will remain unchanged.
>
> • **Fund Term:** The term of the Fund will remain as set forth in the LPA, expiring on **December 31, 2029**, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the General Partner.
>
> • **Portfolio Company Management:** The day-to-day management, board oversight, and operational improvement activities for each of the Fund\'s **11 active portfolio companies** will continue without interruption. The responsibilities of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask with respect to specific portfolio companies have been identified and will be transitioned to other members of the investment team (principally Mr. Hsiao, Ms. Marchetti, and Mr. Okonkwo) in an orderly fashion during the transition periods described in Section 3.3 above.
>
> • **Service Providers:** The Fund\'s existing relationships with its service providers will remain unchanged, including:
>
> • **Heathrow Whitman & Co.** --- auditor and tax advisor
>
> • **Broadleaf Consulting Group** --- independent valuation advisor
>
> • **Pemberton Hale LLP** --- fund counsel

The Management Company will continue to employ **62 professionals** across its investment, operations, finance, legal, compliance, and investor relations functions. No reduction in headcount is anticipated in connection with the Restructuring, and the General Partner is actively recruiting additional investment professionals to support the Fund\'s activities during the remainder of the investment period and beyond.

The SEC **Form ADV** for Ardent Capital Management LLC (CRD #298417) will be amended to reflect the updated ownership structure and personnel changes resulting from the Restructuring. The General Partner anticipates filing the amended Form ADV within **30 days** of the closing of the Restructuring and will provide a copy of the amended Form ADV to any limited partner that requests it.

**[7. Consent Requested]{.underline}**

Pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, the General Partner respectfully requests that each member of the LPAC consent to each of the following actions in connection with the Restructuring:

> 1\. **Formation of New Entities.** The formation of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\") and Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\") as new Delaware limited liability companies, with HoldCo to serve as the parent holding company and GP Intermediate to serve as an intermediate holding entity between HoldCo and the General Partner, as described in Section 3.2 of this letter.
>
> 2\. **Amendment of GP Operating Agreement.** The amendment and restatement of the Limited Liability Company Agreement of Ardent Capital GP III LLC to reflect (a) the withdrawal of David Kellner and Joanna Trask as members, (b) the substitution of GP Intermediate as the sole member of the General Partner, and (c) such other conforming changes as are necessary or appropriate in connection with the Restructuring.
>
> 3\. **Amendment of ManCo Operating Agreement.** The amendment and restatement of the Limited Liability Company Agreement of Ardent Capital Management LLC to reflect HoldCo as the sole member of the Management Company and such other conforming changes as are necessary or appropriate in connection with the Restructuring.
>
> 4\. **Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.** The execution and delivery of **Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership** of Ardent Capital Partners III LP, reflecting the structural changes to the General Partner and the Management Company described herein, including updated definitions, representations, and organizational chart references, as necessary to conform the LPA to the post-Restructuring organizational structure.
>
> 5\. **Economics Realignment.** The reallocation of carried interest percentages and Management Company profit-share economics among the remaining and next-generation principals of the General Partner, as described in Section 3.4 of this letter and summarized in the economics table set forth therein.
>
> 6\. **Departures and Separations.** The departures of David Kellner and Joanna Trask from their respective roles as principals of the General Partner and the Management Company, and the terms of their respective separation arrangements (including carried interest retention, forfeiture, clawback modifications, restrictive covenants, and, in the case of Ms. Trask, the lump-sum separation payment), as described in Section 3.3 of this letter.

Consent may be delivered by execution and return of the enclosed **Form of Written Consent** to the attention of Marcus Aldridge or Nicholas Stern at the addresses set forth in Section 11 below, or by affirmative vote at the LPAC meeting scheduled for February 14, 2024. Under Section 9.4(c) of the LPA, the affirmative consent of a majority of the members of the LPAC (i.e., at least three of the four current LPAC members) is required for each of the actions described above.

**[8. LPAC Meeting]{.underline}**

The General Partner proposes to hold a virtual meeting of the LPAC on **February 14, 2024** (the \"**LPAC Meeting**\") to discuss the Restructuring in detail, to respond to questions from LPAC members, and to receive LPAC consent to the actions described in Section 7 above.

Dial-in and videoconference details for the LPAC Meeting will be provided under separate cover no later than February 9, 2024. The General Partner anticipates that the LPAC Meeting will last approximately 90 minutes to two hours.

The following representatives of the General Partner and its counsel will be available to present the enclosed LPAC Presentation Memorandum and to answer questions at the LPAC Meeting:

> • **Marcus Aldridge**, Co-Founder & Managing Partner, Ardent Capital
>
> • **Priya Narayanan**, Co-Founder & Managing Partner, Ardent Capital
>
> • **Nicholas Stern**, Responsible Partner, Calderwood & Harkness LLP
>
> • **Owen Fischer**, Lead Associate, Calderwood & Harkness LLP

LPAC members are encouraged to submit any questions or requests for additional information in advance of the LPAC Meeting to facilitate a productive and efficient discussion. Advance questions may be directed to Nicholas Stern or Owen Fischer at the contact information set forth in Section 11 below.

**[9. Enclosed Materials]{.underline}**

The following materials are enclosed with this letter for the review and consideration of each LPAC member:

> 1\. **LPAC Presentation Memorandum** --- A detailed summary of the Restructuring, including pre- and post-restructuring organizational charts, economics tables, departing principal terms, key-person analysis, and side-letter compliance summary. This memorandum is intended to serve as a comprehensive reference document for LPAC members and will also form the basis of the presentation at the LPAC Meeting.
>
> 2\. **Form of Written Consent** --- A form of written consent for execution by each LPAC member, consenting to each of the actions described in Section 7 of this letter. LPAC members who wish to deliver their consent in advance of the LPAC Meeting may do so by executing and returning the Form of Written Consent to Marcus Aldridge or Nicholas Stern at the addresses set forth in Section 11 below.

**[10. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

The General Partner reminds each member of the LPAC that the information contained in this letter and the enclosed materials is **confidential and proprietary** to Ardent Capital and its principals. This letter, the enclosed materials, and all information contained herein and therein constitute \"Confidential Information\" within the meaning of Section 11.2 of the LPA and the confidentiality provisions of each LPAC member\'s respective side letter.

The General Partner respectfully requests that each LPAC member treat this letter and all enclosed materials in strict confidence and in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set forth in the LPA and the applicable side letter. This letter and the enclosed materials should not be disclosed, distributed, or made available to any third party (other than the LPAC member\'s own legal, tax, and investment advisors who have a need to know and who are bound by obligations of confidentiality) without the prior written consent of the General Partner.

**[11. Contact Information and Questions]{.underline}**

LPAC members who have questions about the Restructuring or who require additional information are encouraged to contact any of the following individuals:

> **Marcus Aldridge** Co-Founder & Managing Partner Ardent Capital 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, NY 10022 Telephone: (212) 555-4100
>

>
> **Owen Fischer** Lead Associate Calderwood & Harkness LLP One Vanderbilt Avenue, 44th Floor New York, NY 10017 Telephone: (212) 555-7245

We appreciate your continued confidence in Ardent Capital and the investment team. The General Partner is committed to managing the Restructuring in a transparent and orderly manner and to ensuring that the interests of the Fund\'s limited partners are fully protected throughout the process. We look forward to discussing the Restructuring with you at the LPAC Meeting on February 14, 2024, and to receiving your consent in connection therewith.

> Very truly yours,

**ARDENT CAPITAL GP III LLC** as General Partner of Ardent Capital Partners III LP
