the entity framework to accommodate the reduced number of principals and the elevation of next-generation professionals. The restructuring is designed to create a durable, institutionalized framework for managing current and future personnel transitions without disruption to Fund operations or investor relationships.

**[B. Governance Enhancement]{.underline}**

Under the current structure, each of the five senior principals holds direct membership interests in both the General Partner (Ardent Capital GP III LLC) and the ManCo (Ardent Capital Management LLC). This parallel ownership structure, while common at the time of the Fund\'s formation, creates significant complexity in governance and economic alignment, particularly in the context of personnel changes. Each departure or addition of a principal requires amendments to the operating agreements of both entities, separate consent processes, and independent economic negotiations at each level.

The proposed restructuring introduces a centralized holding company --- Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\") --- that will serve as the sole member of both the ManCo and a newly formed intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC. GP Intermediate will, in turn, serve as the sole member of the General Partner. This two-tier governance framework centralizes all ownership and governance authority in HoldCo, creating a single point of control and simplifying future changes. Personnel transitions, economic reallocations, and governance modifications can be effectuated through amendments to the HoldCo LLC Agreement alone, without the need for parallel amendments to the operating agreements of the General Partner and the ManCo.

The restructuring also formalizes decision-making authority. Under the current structure, each principal has equal governance rights proportional to their membership interests in both the GP and the ManCo, which has at times resulted in ambiguity regarding approval requirements for routine operational matters. The HoldCo LLC Agreement designates Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan as Managing Members with authority over day-to-day operations, while reserving certain material actions for supermajority consent of all HoldCo members. This clear delineation of authority is intended to enhance operational efficiency and reduce administrative burden.

**[C. Next-Generation Integration]{.underline}**

A critical objective of the restructuring is the formal integration of two next-generation principals into the Ardent platform\'s economic and governance framework:

> **Elena Marchetti** (Principal, age 38) joined Ardent Capital in 2017 and has been a key contributor to the Fund\'s investment activities, including serving as the primary deal lead on two active portfolio companies. Ms. Marchetti has demonstrated strong investment judgment and leadership capabilities, and her promotion to a carry-bearing role is viewed by the General Partner as an important step in ensuring the platform\'s continuity.
>
> **Samuel Okonkwo** (Principal, age 36) joined Ardent Capital in 2018 and has played an increasingly significant role in the Fund\'s deal origination and portfolio management activities. Mr. Okonkwo has been responsible for sourcing three of the Fund\'s eleven active investments and has earned the confidence of the senior leadership team through his analytical rigor and operational expertise.

Under the proposed restructuring, Ms. Marchetti and Mr. Okonkwo will each receive a 4% carried interest allocation in the Fund and corresponding membership interests in HoldCo. Their economic participation will be subject to vesting schedules set forth in the HoldCo LLC Agreement, which are designed to align their incentives with long-term performance and retention. The General Partner believes that formalizing the economic participation of these next-generation professionals is essential to the institutional stability of the Ardent platform and to retaining top-tier talent in a competitive market for private equity professionals.

**[III. New Entity Structure]{.underline}**

**[A. Current Structure (Pre-Restructuring)]{.underline}**

Under the Fund\'s existing organizational framework, five individual principals hold direct membership interests in both the General Partner and the ManCo:

> **Ardent Capital GP III LLC** (the \"General Partner\") is a Delaware limited liability company and the sole general partner of the Fund. Its members are the five individual principals, each holding membership interests in the following percentages:
>
> • Marcus Aldridge: 35%
>
> • Priya Narayanan: 30%
>
> • David Kellner: 15%
>
> • Joanna Trask: 12%
>
> • Robert Hsiao: 8%
>
> **Ardent Capital Management LLC** (the \"ManCo\") is a Delaware limited liability company that serves as the Fund\'s investment adviser and manager. The ManCo is registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as an investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (CRD #298417). Its members are the same five individual principals, holding membership interests in identical percentages to those set forth above.

The General Partner is the sole general partner of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the Fund). The ManCo provides investment advisory and management services to the Fund pursuant to the terms of the Investment Management Agreement entered into at the time of the Fund\'s formation.

The parallel ownership structure described above --- in which each principal holds identical percentage interests in both the GP and the ManCo --- was established at the time of the Fund\'s formation for simplicity and to align the principals\' economic and governance interests across both entities. However, as discussed in Section II.B above, this structure has proven cumbersome in the context of personnel changes and does not provide an efficient mechanism for the admission of new carry-bearing professionals.

**[B. Proposed Structure (Post-Restructuring)]{.underline}**

Following the restructuring, the organizational framework will be as follows:

> **Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\")** --- a newly formed Delaware limited liability company --- will serve as the parent holding company for the Ardent platform. HoldCo will be the sole member of both the ManCo (directly) and GP Intermediate (directly). The Certificate of Formation for HoldCo was filed with the Delaware Secretary of State on March 1, 2024 (DE File No. 7948231).
>
> The members of HoldCo and their respective membership interests will be as follows:
>
> • Marcus Aldridge: 42%
>
> • Priya Narayanan: 36%
>
> • Robert Hsiao: 14%
>
> • Elena Marchetti: 4%
>
> • Samuel Okonkwo: 4%
>
> **Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\")** --- a newly formed Delaware limited liability company --- will serve as an intermediate entity between HoldCo and the General Partner. GP Intermediate will be the sole member of Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the General Partner). The Certificate of Formation for GP Intermediate was filed with the Delaware Secretary of State on March 1, 2024 (DE File No. 7948237).
>
> **Ardent Capital GP III LLC** (the General Partner) will remain in existence as a Delaware limited liability company and will continue to serve as the sole general partner of the Fund. The only change is that its sole member will be GP Intermediate (replacing the five individual principals). The LLC agreement of the General Partner will be amended and restated (Second Amended and Restated LLC Agreement) to reflect this change in membership.
>
> **Ardent Capital Management LLC** (the ManCo) will remain in existence as a Delaware limited liability company and will continue to serve as the Fund\'s SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD #298417). Its sole member will be HoldCo (replacing the five individual principals). The LLC agreement of the ManCo will be amended and restated (Second Amended and Restated LLC Agreement) to reflect this change in membership. Form ADV will be amended to reflect the new ownership structure.
>
> **Ardent Capital Partners III LP** (the Fund) will remain in existence as a Delaware limited partnership. Ardent Capital GP III LLC will continue to serve as its sole general partner. The Fund\'s LPA will be amended (Amendment No. 1 to the LPA) to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner\'s ownership.

The key structural features of the proposed framework are summarized below:

> • HoldCo is formed as a Delaware limited liability company. Its Certificate of Formation has been filed with the Delaware Secretary of State (filed March 1, 2024, DE File No. 7948231).
>
> • GP Intermediate is formed as a Delaware limited liability company. Its Certificate of Formation has been filed with the Delaware Secretary of State (filed March 1, 2024, DE File No. 7948237).
>
> • The registered agent for both HoldCo and GP Intermediate is Prestige Registered Agents LLC, 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201, Dover, DE 19904.
>
> • HoldCo has been assigned EIN 93-1847225 by the Internal Revenue Service. GP Intermediate has been assigned EIN 93-1847231.
>
> • The ManCo will remain an SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD #298417). An amended Form ADV Part 1 will be filed with the SEC to reflect the new ownership structure, including the identification of HoldCo as the ManCo\'s sole member and the updated Schedule A and Schedule B information. The amendment is targeted for filing on or about March 10, 2024.
>
> • The Managing Members of HoldCo will be Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan, who will have authority over the day-to-day operations of HoldCo and, by extension, the ManCo and the General Partner.
>
> • The departing principals (David Kellner and Joanna Trask) will withdraw as members of both the General Partner and the ManCo. Ardent GP Intermediate LLC will be substituted as the sole member of the General Partner, and HoldCo will be substituted as the sole member of the ManCo.

Organizational charts depicting the current structure (pre-restructuring) and the proposed structure (post-restructuring) are attached hereto as Appendix A and Appendix B, respectively.

**[C. Governance Provisions of HoldCo]{.underline}**

The HoldCo LLC Agreement, which will govern the internal affairs of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC, includes the following key governance provisions:

**Managing Members.** Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan will serve as the Managing Members of HoldCo, with authority over the day-to-day management and operations of HoldCo, the ManCo, and the General Partner. The Managing Members will have the power to act on behalf of HoldCo in all matters arising in the ordinary course of business, including the execution of contracts, the hiring and termination of personnel, the management of portfolio company investments, and the conduct of investor relations.

**Supermajority Consent Provisions.** Certain material actions will require the affirmative consent of members holding at least 75% of the total membership interests in HoldCo (a \"Supermajority Consent\"). Actions requiring Supermajority Consent include, among others:

> \(a\) the transfer, assignment, pledge, or encumbrance of any membership interest in HoldCo;
>
> \(b\) the admission of any new member to HoldCo;
>
> \(c\) any amendment to the carried interest allocation percentages set forth in the Carried Interest Allocation Agreement;
>
> \(d\) the incurrence of any indebtedness by HoldCo, the ManCo, or the General Partner in excess of \$500,000 in the aggregate;
>
> \(e\) the entry into any transaction with an affiliate of HoldCo or any member thereof;
>
> \(f\) the dissolution, liquidation, or winding up of HoldCo, the ManCo, or the General Partner; and
>
> \(g\) any amendment to the HoldCo LLC Agreement.

**Transfer Restrictions.** The HoldCo LLC Agreement contains customary restrictions on the transfer of membership interests. No member may transfer, assign, pledge, or otherwise dispose of any membership interest without the prior written consent of the Managing Members and, in the case of transfers to third parties, a Supermajority Consent. Permitted transfers to immediate family members and estate planning vehicles are subject to the prior written consent of the Managing Members and compliance with applicable securities laws.

**Buy-Sell Provisions.** The HoldCo LLC Agreement includes buy-sell provisions that are triggered upon the occurrence of certain events, including the death, disability, or termination of a member. Upon the occurrence of a triggering event, the remaining members (or HoldCo itself, at the election of the Managing Members) will have the right to purchase the departing member\'s interest at a price determined by a formula-based valuation methodology set forth in the LLC Agreement.

**Tag-Along and Drag-Along Rights.** The HoldCo LLC Agreement includes customary tag-along and drag-along provisions. If the Managing Members propose to transfer more than 50% of their combined membership interests in HoldCo to a third party, each non-Managing Member will have the right to participate in such transfer on a pro rata basis and on the same terms and conditions (tag-along). Conversely, if the Managing Members receive a bona fide offer to acquire 100% of the membership interests in HoldCo, they will have the right to require all other members to participate in such transfer on the same terms and conditions (drag-along).

**Vesting Schedules for Next-Generation Principals.** The membership interests of Elena Marchetti and Samuel Okonkwo in HoldCo will be subject to vesting schedules set forth in the HoldCo LLC Agreement. The specific vesting terms are under negotiation and are expected to include a four-year vesting period with a one-year cliff, subject to continued employment with the ManCo and satisfaction of applicable performance conditions. Unvested interests will be subject to forfeiture upon termination of employment, except in cases of death, disability, or termination without cause.

**[IV. Economics Realignment]{.underline}**

The restructuring necessitates a comprehensive realignment of the Fund\'s economic arrangements, including carried interest allocations, management company profit share distributions, and GP commitment obligations. This section describes the pre-restructuring and post-restructuring economics in detail.

**[A. Pre-Restructuring Carry Allocation]{.underline}**

Under the current carried interest allocation framework, the Fund\'s 20% carried interest (subject to the 8% preferred return and full catch-up mechanism described in Articles VI and VII of the LPA) is allocated among the five senior principals in the following percentages:

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **Current Carry %**     **Accrued Carry (Based on \$87.6M Total)**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- --------------------------------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         35%                     \$30,660,000

  Priya Narayanan         30%                     \$26,280,000

  David Kellner           15%                     \$13,140,000

  Joanna Trask            12%                     \$10,512,000

  Robert Hsiao            8%                      \$7,008,000

  **Total**               **100%**                **\$87,600,000**
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The carried interest rate is 20% of net profits generated by the Fund, calculated on a whole-fund basis, subject to an 8% per annum compounded preferred return to the limited partners and a full (100%) catch-up to the General Partner until the 20/80 split is achieved, all as set forth in Article VII of the LPA. The clawback obligation under the LPA is joint and several among all members of the General Partner, with each individual principal maintaining an escrow account equal to 30% of aggregate carried interest distributions received.

**[B. Post-Restructuring Carry Allocation]{.underline}**

Following the restructuring, the carried interest allocations will be realigned as follows:

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **New Carry %**         **Change from Current**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -------------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         42%                     +7 percentage points

  Priya Narayanan         36%                     +6 percentage points

  Robert Hsiao            14%                     +6 percentage points

  Elena Marchetti         4%                      New allocation

  Samuel Okonkwo          4%                      New allocation

  **Total**               **100%**                ---
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------

The aggregate 27 percentage points of carried interest freed up by the departures of David Kellner (15%) and Joanna Trask (12%) are redistributed among the remaining and next-generation principals as set forth above. The redistribution reflects the General Partner\'s assessment of each principal\'s relative contribution to the Fund\'s investment activities, leadership responsibilities, and long-term commitment to the Ardent platform.

For illustrative purposes, the following table sets forth the notional shares of the \$87.6 million of accrued carried interest (as of September 30, 2023) under the post-restructuring allocation percentages:

It is important to note, however, that the accrued carried interest attributable to the vested interests of David Kellner and Joanna Trask will be carved out and addressed separately pursuant to their respective separation agreements, as described in Section V below. The redistribution of carry percentages described in this Section IV.B applies to go-forward carried interest on future appreciation of the Fund\'s portfolio and on future realizations. The Amended and Restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement will contain detailed provisions governing the allocation of carried interest between the departing principals\' retained vested interests and the post-restructuring allocations.

The carried interest rate (20%), preferred return (8%), catch-up mechanism, and clawback mechanics are unchanged. There is no modification to any economic term of the LPA that affects the limited partners\' rights, including the preferred return, the distribution waterfall, or the clawback.

**[C. Management Fee Allocation]{.underline}**

The Fund\'s annual management fee during the investment period is 1.75% of total committed capital, yielding annual management fee revenue of approximately \$49 million (\$2.8 billion × 1.75%). Following the expiration of the investment period on June 30, 2025, the management fee will step down to 1.50% of invested capital (net of write-offs and write-downs), as provided in Section 4.1 of the LPA.

The ManCo\'s operating expenses --- including compensation and benefits for sixty-two (62) non-principal employees, office lease payments (590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor, New York, NY 10022), technology infrastructure and systems, compliance and regulatory costs, professional liability insurance, and other general and administrative expenses --- total approximately \$31.85 million per annum, representing approximately 65% of the annual management fee revenue.

The ManCo Profit Share --- the residual management fee revenue after payment of operating expenses --- is approximately \$17.15 million per annum (approximately 35% of the \$49 million annual management fee). This profit share is distributed to the principals in accordance with their respective ownership interests in the ManCo (and, following the restructuring, through their membership interests in HoldCo).

**Pre-Restructuring Profit Share Allocation:**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **Share %**             **Annual Amount**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         35%                     \$6,002,500

  Priya Narayanan         30%                     \$5,145,000

  David Kellner           15%                     \$2,572,500

  Joanna Trask            12%                     \$2,058,000

  Robert Hsiao            8%                      \$1,372,000

  **Total**               **100%**                **\$17,150,000**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Post-Restructuring Profit Share Allocation (through HoldCo):**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **Share %**             **Annual Amount**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         42%                     \$7,203,000

  Priya Narayanan         36%                     \$6,174,000

  Robert Hsiao            14%                     \$2,401,000

  Elena Marchetti         4%                      \$686,000

  Samuel Okonkwo          4%                      \$686,000

  **Total**               **100%**                **\$17,150,000**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

There is no change to the management fee rate charged to the Fund, the total management fee amount payable by the limited partners, or the ManCo\'s operating expense budget. The redistribution of the ManCo profit share is an internal economic matter among the principals and does not affect the Fund or its limited partners. The management fee payable by the limited partners under Section 4.1 of the LPA remains \$49 million per annum during the investment period (subject to adjustments for new closings and defaulting limited partners as provided therein).

**[D. GP Commitment Reallocation]{.underline}**

The General Partner\'s aggregate commitment to the Fund is \$42 million, representing 1.5% of the Fund\'s \$2.8 billion in total commitments, as required by Section 3.2 of the LPA. This commitment is funded pro rata by the individual principals in proportion to their membership interests in the General Partner.

The departing principals\' GP commitment obligations are summarized as follows:

> **David Kellner:**
>
> • Total GP commitment: \$6,300,000 (15% × \$42,000,000)
>
> • Funded amount (70%): \$4,410,000
>
> • Unfunded balance: \$1,890,000
>
> **Joanna Trask:**
>
> • Total GP commitment: \$5,040,000 (12% × \$42,000,000)
>
> • Funded amount (70%): \$3,528,000
>
> • Unfunded balance: \$1,512,000
>
> **Combined unfunded departing commitment:** \$3,402,000 (\$1,890,000 + \$1,512,000)

The unfunded balance of the departing principals\' GP commitments (\$3,402,000 in the aggregate) will be assumed by the remaining HoldCo members on a pro rata basis in accordance with their post-restructuring membership percentages:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principal**           **HoldCo %**            **Assumed Unfunded Commitment**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- ---------------------------------
  Marcus Aldridge         42%                     \$1,428,840

  Priya Narayanan         36%                     \$1,224,720

  Robert Hsiao            14%                     \$476,280

  Elena Marchetti         4%                      \$136,080

  Samuel Okonkwo          4%                      \$136,080

  **Total**               **100%**                **\$3,402,000**
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The funded portion of the departing principals\' GP commitments (\$4,410,000 for Kellner and \$3,528,000 for Trask, totaling \$7,938,000) remains invested in the Fund. The economic interest attributable to these funded amounts --- including distributions of investment proceeds --- will follow the carry retention and forfeiture provisions set forth in the respective separation agreements, as described in Section V below. To the extent that Kellner retains 100% of his vested carry and Trask retains 60% of her vested carry, distributions attributable to their funded GP cchetti and Mr. Okonkwo, who have been closely involved in the relevant investments since inception.

**[B. Management Fee]{.underline}**

There is no change to the management fee rate charged to the Fund. The management fee during the investment period remains 1.75% of committed capital (\$49 million per annum). Following the expiration of the investment period on June 30, 2025, the management fee will step down to 1.50% of invested capital, as provided in Section 4.1 of the LPA. The total annual management fee revenue payable by the limited partners is unchanged. The internal allocation of ManCo profit share among the principals (as described in Section IV.C above) is a matter of internal economics and does not affect the amount of the management fee payable by the limited partners.

**[C. Fund Term]{.underline}**

The Fund\'s term remains December 31, 2029, subject to two one-year extensions at the General Partner\'s discretion, as provided in Section 10.1 of the LPA. The restructuring does not modify or otherwise affect the Fund\'s term or extension provisions.

**[D. Investment Team Continuity]{.underline}**

The Fund\'s investment team will continue to be led by the platform\'s co-founders and Managing Partners:

> • **Marcus Aldridge** (Co-Founder & Managing Partner) will continue to devote substantially all of his business time and attention to the Fund and the Ardent platform. Mr. Aldridge is a designated Key Person under Section 5.2 of the LPA.
>
> • **Priya Narayanan** (Co-Founder & Managing Partner) will continue to devote substantially all of her business time and attention to the Fund and the Ardent platform. Ms. Narayanan is a designated Key Person under Section 5.2 of the LPA.
>
> • **Robert Hsiao** (Partner) will continue in his current role, providing investment leadership and portfolio oversight.
>
> • **Elena Marchetti** (Principal) will assume expanded responsibilities as a carry-bearing member of the investment team, reflecting her existing contributions to the Fund\'s investment activities and her demonstrated leadership capabilities.
>
> • **Samuel Okonkwo** (Principal) will similarly assume expanded responsibilities as a carry-bearing member of the investment team, consistent with his growing contributions to deal origination and portfolio management.

The ManCo\'s sixty-two (62) professional employees --- including investment professionals, operations and finance staff, investor relations personnel, legal and compliance professionals, and administrative staff --- remain employed by the ManCo, and no other personnel changes are anticipated in connection with the restructuring. The General Partner is committed to maintaining the depth and stability of the investment team and support infrastructure that the Fund\'s limited partners have relied upon since the Fund\'s formation.

**[E. Service Providers --- No Change]{.underline}**

The Fund\'s key service providers will remain unchanged in connection with the restructuring:

> • **Fund Formation Counsel:** Pemberton Hale LLP (Victoria Langford, partner), One Liberty Plaza, 40th Floor, New York, NY 10006. Pemberton Hale continues to serve as counsel for routine fund operations and will not be replaced.
>
> • **Auditor / Tax Advisor:** Heathrow Whitman & Co. (Paul Devereux, CPA). Heathrow Whitman has served as the Fund\'s independent auditor and tax advisor since formation and continues in that capacity.
>
> • **Valuation Advisor:** Broadleaf Consulting Group (Martin Schreiber, ASA). Broadleaf continues to provide independent valuation advisory services in connection with the Fund\'s quarterly portfolio valuations.
>
> • **Placement Agent:** Lockwood Placement Partners LLC (Sarah Fontaine). Lockwood served as the Fund\'s placement agent during the fundraising period. Tail-fee obligations continue pursuant to the existing Placement Agent Agreement and are unaffected by the restructuring.
>
> • **Restructuring Counsel:** Calderwood & Harkness LLP (Nicholas Stern, responsible partner) has been engaged specifically for the restructuring matter and is the author of this memorandum. Calderwood & Harkness does not serve as the Fund\'s ongoing legal counsel and will not replace Pemberton Hale in that role.

**[VII. Key-Person Analysis]{.underline}**

**[A. LPA Key-Person Provisions (Section 5.2)]{.underline}**

Section 5.2 of the LPA designates Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan as the \"Key Persons\" of the Fund. Under Section 5.2, a \"Key Person Event\" is triggered if:

> \(a\) both Key Persons cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund; or
>
> \(b\) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund and is not replaced by a substitute approved by the LPAC within one hundred twenty (120) days of such cessation.

Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the Fund\'s investment period is automatically suspended, and the General Partner may not make new investments (other than follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies and investments for which binding commitments have been entered into prior to the Key Person Event) until either (i) the LPAC approves a substitute Key Person, or (ii) the LPAC waives the Key Person Event by affirmative vote.

Neither David Kellner nor Joanna Trask is a designated Key Person under Section 5.2 of the LPA. Their departures do not, individually or in combination, constitute a Key Person Event under the LPA.

**Conclusion:** No Key Person Event is triggered by the departures of David Kellner and Joanna Trask. Both designated Key Persons --- Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan --- continue in their full-time roles as Managing Partners of the Ardent platform and will continue to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund.

**[B. Expanded Key-Person Provisions in Side Letters]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding the absence of a Key Person Event under the LPA, certain side letters contain \"expanded key person\" provisions that extend the scope of the key person framework beyond the two designated Key Persons.

Six (6) of the Fund\'s fourteen (14) side letters contain expanded key person provisions that designate David Kellner as a \"Contributing Person.\" Under these side letter provisions, the departure of a Contributing Person triggers the following requirements:

> \(a\) **Notification Requirement:** The General Partner is required to provide written notification to the affected limited partner within fifteen (15) business days of the Contributing Person\'s departure or announcement of departure.
>
> \(b\) **Investment Period Suspension Right:** Three (3) of the six side letters containing expanded key person provisions grant the affected limited partner the right to request a suspension of the Fund\'s investment period for a period of ninety (90) days, during which time the LPAC will review the circumstances of the departure and determine whether any further action is warranted.

The General Partner has taken the following steps to comply with these side letter provisions:

> • Notification letters will be sent to each of the six affected limited partners within fifteen (15) business days of the announcement of Mr. Kellner\'s retirement, in compliance with the notification requirements of their respective side letters.
>
> • With respect to the three side letters that grant an investment period suspension right, the General Partner believes that the LPAC\'s consent to the restructuring, the orderly and planned nature of Mr. Kellner\'s retirement, his continued involvement with the platform as a Senior Advisor for a period of two years, and the promotion of Ms. Marchetti and Mr. Okonkwo to carry-bearing roles should address any concerns and obviate the need for any suspension of the investment period. The General Partner intends to engage proactively with the affected limited partners to discuss these matters and to respond to any questions or concerns.

The General Partner notes that Joanna Trask is not designated as a Contributing Person in any side letter, and accordingly her departure does not trigger any expanded key person provisions.

**[VIII. Side-Letter Compliance Summary]{.underline}**

**[A. Overview]{.underline}**

The Fund has fourteen (14) side letters currently in effect, covering a subset of the Fund\'s forty-seven (47) limited partners. Calderwood & Harkness LLP, in coordination with Pemberton Hale LLP (as the Fund\'s formation counsel), has conducted a comprehensive review of all fourteen side letters to identify any provisions that are implicated by the proposed restructuring.

**[B. Category-by-Category Analysis]{.underline}**

The following is a summary of the side letter provisions reviewed, organized by category, together with an assessment of the impact of the restructuring on each:

**1. Most Favored Nation (\"MFN\") Provisions (11 side letters):**

Eleven of the fourteen side letters contain MFN provisions entitling the applicable limited partner to receive the benefit of any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner (subject to customary carve-outs for terms related to tax, regulatory, or legal requirements specific to a particular investor). Calderwood & Harkness has reviewed the restructuring and has determined that no new \"most favored\" terms are being created by the restructuring that would trigger MFN obligations. The restructuring is an internal organizational matter among the principals and the General Partner and does not modify, amend, or supplement any term of any side letter or the LPA in a manner that would give rise to an MFN claim. No issues have been identified with respect to MFN compliance.

**2. Expanded Key-Person Provisions (6 side letters, naming Kellner as Contributing Person):**

As discussed in detail in Section VII.B above, six side letters contain expanded key person provisions designating David Kellner as a Contributing Person. Written notification to the affected limited partners is required within fifteen (15) business days of Mr. Kellner\'s departure, and three of the six side letters grant a ninety (90)-day investment period suspension right. The General Partner is taking all required actions to comply with these provisions.

**3. Fee discount or Rebate Provisions (8 side letters):**

Eight side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner a discount on management fees or a rebate of a portion of management fees (in each case, subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the applicable side letter). The restructuring does not affect the management fee rate, the total management fee amount, or the calculation methodology for any fee discount or rebate. Accordingly, no fee discount or rebate provision is implicated by the restructuring, and no issues have been identified.

**4. Transfer/Restructuring Consent Requirements (4 side letters):**

Four side letters --- those entered into with the following limited partners --- contain provisions requiring prior written notice and, in certain cases, affirmative consent for any \"material change in the management structure\" of the Fund:

> \(a\) Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System
>
> \(b\) Pinnacle Insurance Group
>
> \(c\) Crestwood Endowment Partners
>
> \(d\) Haverford Capital Partners

LPAC notification letters were sent on February 5, 2024 to each of these limited partners, to the extent they have designated representatives on the LPAC:

> • Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System --- Thomas Engström, Chief Investment Officer
>
> • Crestwood Endowment Partners --- Annika Johansson, Director of Private Equity
>
> • Pinnacle Insurance Group --- Derek Mallinson, Head of Alternatives
>
> • Graystone Family Office LLC --- Catherine Whitfield, Managing Director (LPAC member; not a party to a side letter with transfer/restructuring consent requirements, but included in LPAC notifications as a matter of course)

Haverford Capital Partners, which is not represented on the LPAC, has been separately notified through direct correspondence with its designated representative. The General Partner believes that the LPAC\'s consent to the restructuring, together with the direct notifications provided to each of the four limited partners, satisfies the consent and notification requirements of their respective side letters. In the event that any of the four limited partners raises an objection or requests additional information, the General Partner will engage with such limited partner to address its concerns promptly and in good faith.

**5. Co-Investment Priority Rights (9 side letters):**

Nine side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner priority rights or preferential access to co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund. The restructuring necessitates an update to the Fund\'s Co-Investment Allocation Policy to reflect the removal of David Kellner and Joanna Trask from co-investment eligibility (as they will no longer be principals of the platform) and the updated allocation percentages for the remaining and next-generation principals. The revised Co-Investment Allocation Policy will be distributed to the ManCo\'s investment team and will be made available to the LPAC upon request. The co-investment priority rights of the nine affected limited partners are not diminished or otherwise adversely affected by the restructuring, and no issues have been identified.

**[C. Conclusion]{.underline}**

The proposed restructuring has been designed and structured to comply with all fourteen (14) side letters currently in effect. Required notifications are being sent within the timeframes prescribed by the applicable side letter provisions. No side-letter provision is anticipated to block or materially impede the restructuring. Calderwood & Harkness LLP will continue to monitor compliance with side-letter obligations throughout the implementation process and will work with Pemberton Hale LLP to ensure that all required actions are completed in a timely manner.

A summary matrix of the fourteen side letters, organized by provision category, is attached hereto as Appendix E.

**[IX. LPAC Consent Requested]{.underline}**

**[A. Basis for Consent Solicitation]{.underline}**

Section 9.4 of the LPA requires the prior consent of the LPAC for certain material actions by the General Partner, including, without limitation, any material change in the management structure of the Fund. The restructuring described in this memorandum --- including the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, the amendment of the LLC agreements of the General Partner and the ManCo, the reallocation of carried interest and profit share among the principals, and the execution of separation agreements with departing principals --- constitutes a \"material change in the management structure\" of the Fund within the meaning of Section 9.4. Accordingly, the General Partner is submitting the restructuring to the LPAC for its review and consent.

**[B. Specific Consents Requested]{.underline}**

The General Partner respectfully requests the LPAC\'s consent to the following specific actions:

> 1\. The formation of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\") and Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\") as part of the restructured entity framework described in Section III.B above.
>
> 2\. The amendment and restatement of the LLC agreement of Ardent Capital GP III LLC (Second Amended and Restated LLC Agreement of Ardent Capital GP III LLC) to reflect Ardent GP Intermediate LLC as the sole member of the General Partner.
>
> 3\. The amendment and restatement of the LLC agreement of Ardent Capital Management LLC (Second Amended and Restated LLC Agreement of Ardent Capital Management LLC) to reflect HoldCo as the sole member of the ManCo.
>
> 4\. The execution of Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Ardent Capital Partners III LP, in substantially the form attached hereto as Appendix G, to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner\'s ownership.
>
> 5\. The reallocation of carried interest and ManCo profit share among the remaining and next-generation principals, as described in Section IV above, including the execution of the Amended and Restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement.
>
> 6\. The approval of the separation terms for David Kellner (retirement) and Joanna Trask (voluntary departure), as described in Section V above, including the carry retention and forfeiture provisions, restrictive covenants, and related terms.
>
> 7\. The authorization of the General Partner to execute all related ancillary documents, instruments, certificates, and agreements as may be necessary or desirable to effectuate the restructuring, including without limitation the HoldCo LLC Agreement, the GP Intermediate LLC Agreement, the Senior Advisor Agreement (Kellner), the Separation Agreement (Trask), the Carry Participation Agreements (Kellner and Trask), and all filings with the Delaware Secretary of State, the SEC, and other governmental authorities.

**[C. Form of Consent]{.underline}**

A form of written consent is enclosed separately for execution by each LPAC member (Appendix F). The consent is structured as a single resolution approving all of the actions described in Section IX.B above. Consent of the LPAC constitutes approval under Section 9.4 of the LPA and, together with the side-letter notifications and consents described in Section VIII above, will satisfy all consent requirements applicable to the restructuring.

The General Partner requests that each LPAC member execute and return the enclosed form of consent on or before the date of the LPAC virtual meeting scheduled for February 14, 2024, or as soon as practicable thereafter. Executed consents may be delivered by email to Nicholas Stern at Calderwood & Harkness LLP (nstern@calderwoodharkness.com), with a copy to Marcus Aldridge (maldridge@ardentcapital.com) and Priya Narayanan (pnarayanan@ardentcapital.com).

**[X. Timeline and Next Steps]{.underline}**

The following table sets forth the anticipated timeline for the implementation of the restructuring:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The General Partner will provide the LPAC with updates on the implementation of the restructuring as material developments occur. LPAC members are encouraged to contact the Managing Partners or Calderwood & Harkness LLP with any questions regarding the timeline or the implementation process.

**[I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF MEMORANDUM]{.underline}**

This memorandum documents the results of the conflicts analysis conducted in connection with the proposed engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"the Firm\" or \"C&H\") by Ardent Capital Management LLC (\"ManCo\") to advise on a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"). The purpose of this memorandum is to memorialize the search methodology, results, and analysis performed pursuant to the Firm\'s conflict-of-interest policies and procedures, and to confirm that no conflict of interest exists that would preclude the Firm from undertaking the proposed engagement.

The conflict check was initiated on October 9, 2023, in advance of executing the engagement letter for this matter. In accordance with Firm policy and applicable Rules of Professional Conduct, no substantive work will commence and no engagement letter will be executed until the conflict check has been completed and cleared by the Firm\'s Office of General Counsel.

The analysis covers all parties identified in the initial organizational call held on October 6, 2023, between Nicholas Stern and Marcus Aldridge, as well as all parties identified in the intake materials subsequently provided by Ardent Capital Management LLC on October 7, 2023. The parties searched include, without limitation, the Fund entities, their principals (both remaining and departing), departing principals and their outside counsel, fund formation counsel, key limited partners (including all Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") members), the Fund\'s placement agent, auditors and tax advisors, valuation advisors, and the Fund\'s registered agent.

The review was conducted against Calderwood & Harkness\'s firm-wide centralized conflicts database (Glenrock Health IT Walls and Greaves Services Inc.), current and historical matter records dating to the Firm\'s founding, individual attorney disclosures (including lateral hire screening records), and personal conflict certifications obtained from each member of the proposed engagement team. The scope of the search extended to all known affiliates, related entities, and prior fund vintages associated with the identified parties.

**[IV. CONFLICT CHECK METHODOLOGY]{.underline}**

The conflict check was conducted in accordance with Calderwood & Harkness\'s Firm Policy No. 4.2 (Conflicts of Interest --- New Engagement Clearance Procedures), as most recently updated on July 1, 2023. The following procedures were followed:

**Database Search.** All party names, entity names, individual names, and known aliases or short names (as set forth in Appendix A) were searched against Calderwood & Harkness\'s centralized conflicts database, maintained through the Glenrock Health IT Walls and Greaves Services Inc. systems. The database captures all current and former client representations, adverse party records, lateral hire conflict disclosures, and financial interest and investment disclosures from all attorneys in the Firm. The search was run on October 9, 2023, at approximately 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, and the results were reviewed and analyzed by the undersigned.

**Current and Historical Matter Records.** In addition to the automated database search, a manual review of current and historical matter records was conducted to identify any representations that may have been entered under variant names or entity designations that might not have been captured by the automated search. This review encompassed the Firm\'s matter management system and billing records.

**Affiliate Cross-References.** Cross-reference searches were conducted for all known affiliates of each identified party. For the Ardent Capital entities, this included searches for prior fund vintages (Ardent Capital Partners I LP, Ardent Capital Partners II LP, and any co-investment vehicles or parallel funds, if any), as well as searches for known portfolio company names where available from public sources. For the limited partners, searches were conducted for known parent entities, subsidiaries, and affiliated investment vehicles.

**Individual Attorney Certifications.** Individual conflict certifications were requested from all members of the proposed engagement team: Nicholas Stern, Graham Sutherland, Owen Fischer, Stephen Adler, and Sylvia Hartwell. Each team member was asked to confirm: (a) whether they have any personal conflict of interest with respect to any identified party; (b) whether they have any financial interest (direct or indirect) in any identified party; (c) whether they have any personal or familial relationship with any individual associated with an identified party; and (d) whether they are aware of any circumstance that could impair their independent professional judgment in connection with the proposed engagement. All five certifications have been received and are documented in Section VI below and attached as Appendix B.

**Scope of Review.** The conflict analysis was conducted with reference to the New York Rules of Professional Conduct, Rules 1.7 (Conflict of Interest --- Current Clients), 1.8 (Current Clients --- Specific Rules), 1.9 (Duties to Former Clients), and 1.10 (Imputation of Conflicts of Interest), as well as the Firm\'s internal conflicts policies, which impose obligations that in certain respects exceed the minimum requirements of the applicable professional conduct rules.

**[VII. ANALYSIS OF POTENTIAL ISSUES]{.underline}**

While the conflict search returned no disqualifying conflicts, the following potential issues were identified and analyzed to confirm that no conflict of interest exists. This analysis is provided for completeness and to document the Firm\'s consideration of relationship dynamics that, while not constituting conflicts, warrant attention and memorialization.

**A. Dual Representation Considerations**

Calderwood & Harkness is engaged by Ardent Capital Management LLC (the ManCo), but the restructuring involves multiple related entities: the Fund, the GP, the ManCo, and the to-be-formed HoldCo and GP Intermediate. All of these entities are under common control by Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan, and their interests are aligned for purposes of this transaction. The restructuring is being undertaken at the direction of the managing members and is designed to benefit all of the related entities by creating a more sustainable organizational structure that facilitates succession planning and economic realignment.

The engagement letter clarifies that Calderwood & Harkness represents the ManCo and, by extension, the GP in connection with the restructuring. The Firm does not represent any individual principal in their personal capacity. This distinction is material because the restructuring will result in changes to the economic interests of individual principals --- specifically, the reallocation of carried interest percentages and management fee economics among remaining and next-generation principals. While the Firm is advising on the structural and documentation aspects of these changes, the economic split among principals (i.e., the specific percentage allocations) has been determined by the principals themselves through internal negotiations. Calderwood & Harkness\'s role is limited to implementing the agreed-upon economics through appropriate legal documentation, not to advocating for any particular allocation on behalf of any individual.

The interests of the remaining principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, and Hsiao) and next-generation principals (Marchetti and Okonkwo) are aligned as to the restructuring itself, though their individual economic interests (allocation percentages) differ. This is a common and well-understood dynamic in management company restructurings and does not give rise to a conflict of interest where, as here, the economic terms have been agreed among the principals prior to the engagement of outside counsel and the Firm\'s role is limited to documentation and structural advice. No conflict arises.

The engagement letter will include appropriate disclaimers confirming that: (i) the Firm represents the ManCo and GP entities, not any individual principal; (ii) individual principals should consult with their own personal counsel regarding the effect of the restructuring on their individual interests; and (iii) the Firm has not provided, and will not provide, advice to any individual principal regarding the fairness or adequacy of any particular economic allocation.

**B. Departing Principals --- Adverse Party Analysis**

The departing principals --- David Kellner (retiring) and Joanna Trask (departing voluntarily) --- are adverse to the ManCo and GP in the negotiation of separation terms. The matters at issue include, without limitation: (a) carried interest retention percentages (i.e., what portion of the departing principals\' current 15% and 12% carried interest allocations, respectively, will be retained, vested, or forfeited upon departure); (b) the terms of any clawback obligations applicable to retained carry; (c) the duration and scope of non-competition and non-solicitation covenants; (d) the terms of any Senior Advisor arrangement for Kellner, including consulting fees, office access, and administrative support; (e) representations and warranties regarding the return of confidential information and firm property; and (f) general release and waiver provisions.

Calderwood & Harkness does not represent and has not represented either Kellner or Trask. Their interests are represented by Whitford & Chase LLP, a reputable firm with a well-established private funds practice. Richard Beaulieu, a partner at Whitford & Chase, will serve as lead counsel for the departing principals, and Hannah Polk, an associate, will support the engagement. The departing principals are sophisticated parties who are represented by competent independent counsel of their own choosing.

No prior relationship exists between Calderwood & Harkness and either departing principal that would impede the Firm from acting adverse to either departing principal in negotiating the separation agreements. No prior representation, no personal relationship, and no financial interest has been identified. The Firm is fully able to advocate zealously on behalf of the ManCo and GP in the separation negotiations without any constraint arising from a prior relationship or obligation to either departing principal.

**C. Fund Formation Counsel Coordination**

Pemberton Hale LLP served as original fund-formation counsel for Fund III, including all organizational and formation documentation, the LPA and ancillary fund documents, side-letter negotiation, and the fundraising process through final close on April 15, 2019. Pemberton Hale continues to serve as counsel for routine fund operations, including portfolio company acquisition and disposition documentation, LP communications, annual meeting preparation, and ongoing regulatory compliance matters.

Calderwood & Harkness is being brought in specifically for the restructuring workstream, which is a discrete, defined engagement separate from Pemberton Hale\'s ongoing mandate. The scope delineation between the two firms is clear and has been discussed with both Victoria Langford of Pemberton Hale and Marcus Aldridge:

> • **Calderwood & Harkness** handles: restructuring documentation (HoldCo and GP Intermediate formation, amended and restated operating agreements, carry allocation agreements), LP consent processes related to the restructuring (LPAC consent under Section 9.4 of the LPA, side-letter compliance, LP notification materials), departing principal separation agreements and related documentation, and SEC Form ADV amendments related to the restructuring.
>
> • **Pemberton Hale LLP** continues with: routine fund operations, portfolio company transactions, ongoing LP communications unrelated to the restructuring, and general regulatory compliance matters.

No conflict of interest arises from the parallel engagement of two law firms on separate workstreams for the same client group. This is a common arrangement in complex private equity restructurings, where specialized expertise may be required for certain workstreams that fall outside the scope of existing fund counsel\'s engagement. The two firms will coordinate and share information as necessary, with appropriate joint-defense and common-interest protections in place.

**D. LP Interests**

While the restructuring requires LPAC consent under Section 9.4 of the LPA and involves notification to all 47 limited partners, the LP interests are not adverse to the GP and ManCo in this context. The restructuring is being undertaken to ensure continuity and stability of the Fund\'s management team, to provide for orderly succession planning, and to align the economic interests of remaining and next-generation principals with the long-term interests of the Fund and its limited partners. The restructuring does not alter the Fund\'s investment strategy, management fee rates, preferred return provisions, distribution waterfall mechanics, or fund term.

Certain side letters --- specifically, four side letters with Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System, Pinnacle Insurance Group, Crestwood Endowment Partners, and Haverford Capital Partners --- contain provisions requiring prior written notice or consent for material changes in the management structure of the GP or ManCo, changes in the identity of \"Key Persons\" (as defined in each respective side letter), or other material organizational changes. Compliance with these side-letter provisions involves procedural notification and consent processes rather than adversarial negotiations. The LP consent process is expected to be cooperative and consent-driven, as the restructuring is being presented as a positive development for the Fund and its limited partners.

Calderwood & Harkness does not represent any limited partner of the Fund. The engagement letter with the ManCo confirms that the Firm\'s representation does not extend to any LP and that the Firm will not provide advice to, or advocate on behalf of, any LP in connection with the restructuring. No conflict exists.

**[3. Summary of Workstreams Completed]{.underline}**

**3.1 Workstream I --- Entity Restructuring**

**3.1.1 Formation of Holding Company Structure.** The centerpiece of the restructuring was the formation of a new two-tier holding company structure to replace the prior arrangement under which five individual principals held direct membership interests in both the GP and ManCo. Under the pre-restructuring arrangement, each of the five principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) held direct ownership percentages in both ManCo and the GP. This structure presented several challenges: (i) the departure of any principal required direct amendments to the governing documents of both ManCo and the GP, together with the re-execution of multiple ancillary agreements; (ii) the admission of new principals similarly required direct amendments at both the ManCo and GP levels; (iii) the platform lacked a centralized governance structure capable of facilitating efficient decision-making and succession planning; and (iv) the direct ownership structure created inefficiencies in connection with tax reporting, capital account administration, and allocation mechanics.

To address these challenges, Calderwood & Harkness designed and implemented a holding company structure consisting of two newly formed Delaware limited liability companies:

**Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\")** was formed as a new Delaware LLC on March 1, 2024, pursuant to a Certificate of Formation filed with the Delaware Secretary of State, Delaware File No. 7948231. The authorized person for the filing was Marcus Aldridge. The registered agent is Prestige Registered Agents LLC, located at 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201, Dover, Delaware 19904. HoldCo\'s EIN is 93-1847225. HoldCo serves as the parent holding company of both ManCo (as its direct sole member) and GP Intermediate (as its direct sole member). The five continuing principals hold their economic and governance interests in HoldCo, which centralizes ownership, governance, and economics at a single entity level.

**Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\")** was formed as a new Delaware LLC on March 1, 2024, pursuant to a Certificate of Formation filed with the Delaware Secretary of State, Delaware File No. 7948237. The authorized person for the filing was Marcus Aldridge. The registered agent is Prestige Registered Agents LLC at the same address. GP Intermediate\'s EIN is 93-1847231. GP Intermediate functions as an intermediate single-member entity between HoldCo and the GP. Its inclusion in the structure serves to provide an additional layer of liability separation between the holding company and the general partner entity, to facilitate future structural flexibility (including the potential admission of additional funds or co-investment vehicles at the GP level), and to preserve certain tax planning optionality identified by Sylvia Hartwell in the tax structuring memorandum.

Under the new structure, the organizational hierarchy is as follows:

> • The five continuing principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Hsiao, Marchetti, and Okonkwo) hold membership interests in HoldCo.
>
> • HoldCo is the sole member of ManCo (directly).
>
> • HoldCo is the sole member of GP Intermediate.
>
> • GP Intermediate is the sole member of the GP.
>
> • The GP is the sole general partner of the Fund.

This structure permits future changes in principal-level ownership, economics, and governance to be accomplished through amendments to the HoldCo LLC Agreement alone, without the need to amend the governing documents of ManCo, the GP, or the Fund (except in circumstances requiring LP notification or consent under the LPA).

**3.1.2 Governing Documents Prepared and Executed.** The following governing documents were prepared, negotiated, and executed in connection with the entity restructuring workstream. All documents were executed as of February 28, 2024, with the new entity formations completed on March 1, 2024:

**Amended and Restated LLC Agreement --- Ardent Capital Holdings LLC.** This agreement establishes the governance, economic, and operational framework for HoldCo and constitutes the principal governing document of the restructured platform. The first draft was circulated to the continuing principals on November 15, 2023, and was finalized after multiple rounds of negotiation among the principals (in particular regarding the allocation percentages and vesting terms for the next-generation principals). The agreement became effective February 28, 2024. Key provisions include:

> • **Membership Interests:** Aldridge (42%), Narayanan (36%), Hsiao (14%), Marchetti (4%), Okonkwo (4%).
>
> • **Managing Members:** Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan serve as co-Managing Members with authority to manage the day-to-day affairs of HoldCo and its subsidiaries, subject to certain reserved matters requiring supermajority approval.
>
> • **Governance:** Includes reserved matter provisions (e.g., admission of new members, amendments to fund documents, new fund formation, indebtedness above certain thresholds, related-party transactions) requiring the affirmative vote of members holding at least 70% of the membership interests.
>
> • **Capital Contributions:** Addresses initial and subsequent capital contribution obligations, including the assumption of departing principal unfunded GP commitment obligations.
>
> • **Distributions:** Establishes the priority and mechanics of distributions from HoldCo, including management fee profit distributions and carried interest pass-through distributions, in each case in accordance with each member\'s membership interest percentage.
>
> • **Transfer Restrictions:** Comprehensive restrictions on transfer of membership interests, including rights of first refusal, mandatory offer-back provisions, and permitted transfer exceptions for estate planning purposes.
>
> • **Buy-Sell Provisions:** Includes cross-purchase, put/call, and tag-along/drag-along mechanics triggered upon specified events (death, disability, termination for cause, voluntary departure, change of control).
>
> • **Vesting Schedules:** The membership interests of the next-generation principals (Marchetti and Okonkwo) are subject to four-year vesting with a one-year cliff, with acceleration upon a change of control or termination without cause.

**LLC Agreement --- Ardent GP Intermediate LLC.** This agreement governs GP Intermediate as a single-member entity wholly owned by HoldCo. The agreement provides for pass-through governance (all governance decisions are made by HoldCo as sole member), pass-through of GP economics to HoldCo, and limited purpose provisions restricting GP Intermediate\'s activities to the holding of the membership interest in the GP and ancillary activities related thereto. The agreement became effective February 28, 2024.

**[4. Tax Analysis Summary]{.underline}**

The tax aspects of the restructuring were addressed by Sylvia Hartwell (Specialist Partner, Tax), with analytical support from Stephen Adler.

A comprehensive **tax structuring memorandum** was delivered to the Client on November 22, 2023. The memorandum analyzed the federal income tax consequences of the proposed restructuring transactions and recommended a structural approach designed to achieve the most tax-efficient outcome for the principals. The key elements of the tax analysis are summarized below:

**HoldCo Formation --- IRC Section 721 Treatment.** The formation of HoldCo was structured as a tax-free contribution of the principals\' membership interests in the GP and ManCo to HoldCo in exchange for membership interests in HoldCo, qualifying for non-recognition treatment under Internal Revenue Code Section 721. Under Section 721, no gain or loss is recognized by the contributing partners or by HoldCo upon the contribution of property (including partnership interests) to a partnership in exchange for an interest in that partnership. This treatment was conditioned on proper documentation and compliance with the requirements of Section 721 and the applicable Treasury Regulations. The tax memorandum concluded that, if properly structured in accordance with the recommended approach, no taxable event would occur at the HoldCo formation level.

**Section 704(b)/704(c) Allocation Analysis.** Stephen Adler, under the supervision of Sylvia Hartwell, prepared a detailed **Section 704(b)/704(c) Allocation Analysis Memorandum** addressing the book-tax disparities arising from the carry reallocation, the treatment of the departing principals\' interests, and the methodology selection for the HoldCo operating agreement\'s allocation provisions. The analysis examined the following issues:

> • **Book-Tax Disparities from Carry Reallocation:** The reallocation of carried interest percentages creates book-tax disparities to the extent that the contributed interests have built-in gain or loss at the time of contribution to HoldCo. The memorandum analyzed the magnitude of these disparities based on the September 30, 2023 valuation data.
>
> • **Treatment of Departing Interests:** The memorandum addressed the tax treatment of the departing principals\' retained carry interests, concluding that such interests retain their character as partnership interests (i.e., as interests in the GP, which in turn holds an interest in the Fund) and are not recharacterized as a result of the restructuring.
>
> • **Methodology Selection:** The memorandum analyzed the relative merits of the traditional method and the remedial allocation method under Treasury Regulations Section 1.704-3 for addressing Section 704(c) allocations within HoldCo. After analysis of the specific facts and circumstances, the memorandum recommended the use of the remedial allocation method as the most appropriate approach for the HoldCo operating agreement, given the complexity of the contributing interests and the desire to achieve precise matching of tax items to economic entitlements.

**Key Tax Conclusions.** The principal tax conclusions of the engagement were as follows:

> 1\. No taxable event at the HoldCo formation level if the contribution is properly structured under IRC Section 721, with appropriate documentation of the contributing partners\' bases in their contributed interests and compliance with the applicable anti-abuse provisions.
>
> 2\. Joanna Trask\'s separation payment of \$1,250,000 is treated as ordinary income to Trask, subject to applicable withholding and reporting requirements. The payment is deductible by ManCo as a business expense in the tax year paid, subject to any applicable limitations.
>
> 3\. Carried interest retained by the departing principals (Kellner: \$13,140,000; Trask: \$6,307,200) retains its character as a partnership interest, and distributions on such retained carry will be taxed to the departing principals in accordance with the character of the underlying Fund income (i.e., capital gains or ordinary income, as applicable) and the provisions of IRC Section 1061 (applicable to carried interests held for less than three years).

All tax conclusions were discussed with the Client and coordinated with Heathrow Whitman & Co. for purposes of ongoing tax compliance and reporting.

No further vote, approval, consent, or other action by any member, manager, officer, or other person is required in connection with the execution, delivery, or performance by the GP of the Restructuring Documents or the consummation of the transactions contemplated thereby.
>
> \(d\) **No Conflict.** The execution and delivery of the Restructuring Documents by the GP, and the consummation by the GP of the transactions contemplated thereby, do not and will not (i) conflict with, or result in any violation or breach of, any provision of the Certificate of Formation or the limited liability company agreement (as amended and restated) of the GP, (ii) conflict with, or result in any violation or breach of, the LPA or any other organizational or governing document of the Fund, (iii) conflict with, or result in any violation or breach of, any applicable law, statute, regulation, rule, judgment, order, decree, or injunction of any governmental authority applicable to the GP, the Fund, or any of their respective properties or assets, or (iv) conflict with, result in any violation or breach of, or constitute a default (with or without notice or lapse of time, or both) under, or result in the acceleration of, or create in any party the right to accelerate, terminate, modify, or cancel any obligation under, any material agreement, contract, lease, instrument, or other arrangement to which the GP or the Fund is a party or by which the GP, the Fund, or any of their respective properties or assets is bound.
>
> \(e\) **Accuracy of Financial Information.** All financial information provided to the limited partners and the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\") of the Fund in connection with the Restructuring, including without limitation the portfolio valuation summary, the carried interest accrual schedule, the management fee reconciliation, and the GP commitment funding schedule, is true, correct, and complete in all material respects as of the dates and for the periods indicated therein. No material facts have been omitted from such financial information that would be necessary to make the statements contained therein, in light of the circumstances under which they were made, not misleading.

**[SECTION 3: CONSENTS OBTAINED]{.underline}**

3.1. The undersigned hereby certifies, on behalf of the GP, that all consents, approvals, and authorizations required to consummate the transactions contemplated by the Restructuring Documents have been duly obtained prior to or as of the date hereof, including without limitation the following:

> \(a\) **LPAC Consent.** The consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee of the Fund was duly obtained at a virtual meeting of the LPAC held on February 14, 2024, pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, which requires the prior consent of the LPAC for any material restructuring of the general partner or management company of the Fund. Notice of the LPAC meeting was provided to all LPAC members in accordance with the notice provisions of the LPA on January 31, 2024, which was not fewer than ten (10) business days prior to the date of the meeting. The following LPAC members attended the meeting and provided their affirmative consent to the Restructuring:
>
> \(i\) Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System, represented by Thomas Engström, Chief Investment Officer;
>
> \(ii\) Crestwood Endowment Partners, represented by Annika Johansson, Director of Private Equity;
>
> \(iii\) Pinnacle Insurance Group, represented by Derek Mallinson, Head of Alternatives; and
>
> \(iv\) Graystone Family Office LLC, represented by Catherine Whitfield, Managing Director.
>
> The consent of the LPAC was unanimous, and no LPAC member dissented from or abstained with respect to the approval of the Restructuring. Minutes of the LPAC meeting were prepared and distributed to LPAC members on February 16, 2024, and copies of such minutes are maintained in the records of the Fund.
>
> \(b\) **Member Consent.** The unanimous written consent of all Members of Ardent Capital GP III LLC --- namely, Marcus Aldridge, Priya Narayanan, David Kellner, Joanna Trask, and Robert Hsiao --- was duly obtained on February 28, 2024, as set forth in the Member Consent Resolutions. The Member Consent Resolutions approved the following matters, among others:
>
> \(i\) the formation of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC as the new holding company for the principals\' economic interests in the GP and the ManCo, and the formation of Ardent GP Intermediate LLC as the sole member of the GP;
>
> \(ii\) the economics realignment, including the reallocation of carried interest and management fee profit sharing among the principals in connection with the Restructuring;
>
> \(iii\) the withdrawal of David Kellner and Joanna Trask as members of Ardent Capital GP III LLC and the acceptance of their resignations from all offices and positions held with the GP and the ManCo;
>
> \(iv\) the admission of Ardent GP Intermediate LLC as the sole member of Ardent Capital GP III LLC following the withdrawal of all individual members;
>
> \(v\) the execution and delivery of all Restructuring Documents on behalf of the GP, and the authorization of the GP to cause the Fund and the ManCo to execute and deliver the Restructuring Documents to which such entities are parties;
>
> \(vi\) the filing of Amendment No. 1 to the LPA with the records of the Fund and the delivery of copies thereof to all limited partners; and
>
> \(vii\) the authorization of Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan, and each of them acting individually, to execute and deliver on behalf of the GP all documents, instruments, certificates, and agreements necessary or desirable to consummate the transactions contemplated by the Restructuring Documents.
>
> \(c\) **Side-Letter Compliance.** The GP has completed a comprehensive review of all fourteen (14) side letters entered into by the Fund with certain limited partners in connection with the Fund\'s initial and subsequent closings. Of the fourteen (14) total side letters, four (4) contain provisions requiring prior written notice of, or affirmative consent to, any \"material change in the management structure\" of the Fund or words of similar import. Notification has been duly provided to, and where required, affirmative consent has been obtained from, each of the following limited partners holding such side letters:
>
> \(i\) Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System;
>
> \(ii\) Pinnacle Insurance Group;
>
> \(iii\) Crestwood Endowment Partners; and
>
> \(iv\) Haverford Capital Partners.
>
> A memorandum summarizing the results of the side-letter compliance review was prepared by Pemberton Hale LLP and finalized on February 22, 2024, and a copy of such memorandum has been provided to Calderwood & Harkness LLP as restructuring counsel. All required notifications and consents under the applicable side letters have been duly provided or obtained, as the case may be, and no limited partner has objected to or challenged the Restructuring in connection with the side-letter compliance process.
>
> \(d\) **Contributing Person Notification.** Timely notification has been provided, within fifteen (15) business days prior to the closing of the Restructuring, to the six (6) limited partners whose side letters contain expanded key-person provisions naming David Kellner as a \"Contributing Person\" (as defined in the applicable side letters). The notification described the nature and expected timing of Mr. Kellner\'s retirement and departure from the management platform, the terms of his Senior Advisor Agreement, and the economic arrangements set forth in his Carry Retention and Clawback Side Letter. No limited partner receiving such notification has exercised any right to suspend or terminate its commitment to the Fund or to request any additional information beyond the information provided in the notification.
>
> \(e\) **No Additional Regulatory or Third-Party Approvals Required.** Other than the amendment to SEC Form ADV for Ardent Capital Management LLC (CRD #298417), which is expected to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on or about March 10, 2024, no additional regulatory consents, approvals, filings, or third-party approvals are required as a condition to the closing of the Restructuring. The Form ADV amendment is not a condition precedent to closing but rather a post-closing compliance obligation that will be satisfied within the applicable regulatory timeframe. The GP confirms that it has consulted with Pemberton Hale LLP regarding all applicable regulatory requirements in connection with the Restructuring and has been advised that no other regulatory filings or approvals are required as a condition to closing.

**[SECTION 4: NO MATERIAL ADVERSE CHANGE]{.underline}**

4.1. The undersigned hereby certifies, on behalf of the GP, that since September 30, 2023, which is the date of the most recent quarterly valuation of the Fund\'s portfolio prepared by Broadleaf Consulting Group (the Fund\'s independent valuation advisor), there has been no material adverse change in the business, operations, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or prospects of any of the following:

> \(a\) Ardent Capital Partners III LP or any of its eleven (11) active portfolio companies;
>
> \(b\) Ardent Capital GP III LLC; or
>
> \(c\) Ardent Capital Management LLC.

4.2. As of September 30, 2023, the key performance metrics of the Fund were as follows:
